body: angr's MIPS-O32 syscall number table in angr/procedures/definitions/linux_kernel.py uses NUMBERS THAT DIFFER from upstream Linux for the *at family. Examples: mkdirat=4289 (upstream 4287), unlinkat=4294 (upstream 4292), renameat=4295 (upstream 4293), readlinkat=4298 (matches upstream), faccessat=4300 (matches upstream). Some match, some are off by +2. Why this matters: native Rust syscall handlers MUST use angr's numbers, not upstream Linux, because angr's SimSyscallLibrary maps syscall names -> numbers via this table, and our dispatcher receives the angr-issued number when a name-based syscall fires. Using upstream numbers would silently de-register the handler for that name. COROLLARY (angr-0jh0j.58): the same table also decides whether a syscall is registerable AT ALL on an arch -- getrandom exists in real Linux on ARM/AArch64/MIPS but has no entry in angr's arm/armhf/aarch64/mips-o32/mips-n64 maps, so NativeGetrandomSyscall is registered only for AMD64 (318) and X86 (355). Before adding a handler row for a new arch, confirm the name is in that arch's dict; 'the Linux ABI has it' is not sufficient. Awk to inspect by arch index: awk '/lib.add_number_mapping_from_dict/{c++} c==N && /<name>/' angr/procedures/definitions/linux_kernel.py where N=1 (aarch64), 2 (amd64), 3 (arm), 4 (armhf), 5 (i386), 6 (mips-n32), 7 (mips-n64), 8 (mips-o32).

Round 8 (bd epic angr-fs8kb, sweep complete 2026-09-13; epic remains OPEN -- bd refuses to close an epic with open children, and 0/88 findings are fixed yet, so it stays open until its children are worked down) swept all of native/angr/src/ (minus the standing automaton/+fuzzer/ descope) across 24 areas (re-partitioned from round 7's 23 to reflect directory growth: exploration/ split into 4, vex/ split into 3, symbolic/ split into 3, procedures/ split into 4, syscalls/ split into 2, interpreter/ split into 2, plus single areas for memory/, state/, arch/, callbacks/, claripy_bridge+solver/, and root-level loose files -- the last two (claripy_bridge/solver and root-core-infra) had NEVER had a dedicated audit pass before this round and both produced real findings, confirming CLAUDE.md's recon-flagged gap was real). Method: sequential (non-parallel, per user's explicit choice) finder-then-independent-verifier pairs per area, same 8 review angles as rounds 5-7 (correctness, DRY, file-org, naming, test-coverage/dead-code, docs-accuracy, PR-reviewability, overflow/width-boundary), one bd bead per CONFIRMED finding only (verifier explicitly re-checked every claim against live code, not the finder's description -- this caught several claimed P1/P2s that were actually latent/unreachable and got downgraded, e.g. a shl_into width>128 bug rated P2 not P1 because unreachable from real VEX dispatch, and a brk.rs finding initially claimed P2 that was fully REFUTED on the core claim after the verifier traced a wraparound-identity coincidence that made it actually work correctly).

Total: 88 findings (2 P1, 9 P2, 39 P3, 38 P4) -- continues the volume trend 239/149/50/83/79/69/86/88 (essentially flat vs round 7, still well above the round-3 floor of 50; round-over-round volume is not a reliable freshness signal on its own, per round 6's and 7's own notes).

Best catches (worth reading in full via bd show if fixing): angr-fs8kb.28 (P1, empirically-reproduced process-abort crash: RustBV::from_parts panics building a 0-width Z3 sort for ANY symbolic BV of width 0 -- reachable via claripy.BVS(name,0), solver-handle-API's create_symbolic(name,0), and snapshot deserialization; found while VERIFYING a different finding, not by a finder -- worth remembering that verifiers can surface net-new bugs, not just confirm/refute); angr-fs8kb.49 (P1, mprotect.rs page-walk bare += silently wraps at the top of the 64-bit address space, guest-reachable via two ordinary syscalls -- ALSO exposed a real gate blind spot, angr-fs8kb.52: audit_overflow_wraparound.py's regex explicitly excludes += / -= compound assignment, so this whole shape is invisible to the gate project-wide, not just untriaged); angr-fs8kb.40 (P2, systemic: ~9 int-returning native SimProcedures across printf/puts/malloc/getopt/fileops/strcmp/fgets/access/rand/system write a narrower-than-register return value without zero-extending the remainder, unlike real hardware -- root-caused down to RegisterFile::put in a LATER area pass this same round, which also found the bug independently exists in put()'s symbolic-overlay branch too, not just the concrete branch, and that the correct fix is NOT a blanket zero-extend in put() itself since al/ah/ax-style sub-registers must NOT zero-extend and MIPS64 needs sign- not zero-extension -- this bead accumulated notes across 3 separate area passes, a good example of the fold-into-existing-bead pattern working as intended instead of bead sprawl); angr-fs8kb.68 (P2, SymbolicMemory::merge loses a cross-page symbolic object's span index when its base page is both-present but tail page is other-only -- same repeat-offender family as rounds 3/6/7's Multi-cell merge bugs, still finding fresh instances); angr-fs8kb.57 (P2, handle_dirty_call's GuardClass::Never arm skips VEX's guaranteed-defined-tmp semantics, confirmed against the actual vendored libvex_ir.h header on this system); angr-fs8kb.71 (P2, state/'s call_stack field merges self_wins with no divergence warning unlike sibling native_resume_stack, despite driving real ret-vs-unmodeled-call classification -- found in the DE-EMPHASIZED state/ area, a reminder that de-emphasizing an area for lighter scrutiny should not mean skipping verification rigor once something real turns up).

Process notes for round 9: (1) the fold-into-existing-bead-via-append-notes pattern (used ~6 times this round for angr-fs8kb.40 and .28) worked well for a bug whose root cause spans multiple areas -- keep doing this rather than filing near-duplicate beads, but ALWAYS bd show the target bead first to get its exact current wording before composing an addition. (2) A citation-drift trap: pre-writing bd create commands that cross-reference bead IDs you're ABOUT to create (predicting sequential numbering) is fragile -- bd assigns IDs at creation time in creation order within one shell invocation, and if any single bd create in a batch fails or reorders, every subsequent guessed ID is wrong. This round it happened twice (mprotect/brk cluster, angr-fs8kb.49/.51/.52) and required a follow-up bd update sweep to fix -- next round, either create beads one at a time when they cross-reference each other, or create them all first without cross-refs and add the cross-refs in one follow-up pass once real IDs are known. (3) Two areas (claripy_bridge/solver.rs, and the root-level loose files under native/angr/src/ not in any subdirectory) had literally never been given a dedicated round pass before -- both were flagged as gaps by this round's own pre-audit recon and both paid off immediately (a P1 crash and a P3 process-abort risk respectively) -- prioritize re-checking these two are still getting covered in round 9 and don't let them silently drop off the rotation again. (4) tools/audit_overflow_wraparound.py has a confirmed, project-wide blind spot for += / -= compound assignment (angr-fs8kb.52) -- if that gate gets extended to catch this shape, re-run it against the whole tree once merged rather than assuming this round's manual finds were exhaustive. (5) bd close on an epic hard-fails while any child is open ('cannot close epic ...: N open child issue(s); close children first or use --force') -- do not assume a just-filed round epic can or should be closed same-day; it closes naturally once its children are worked down, matching what actually happened with round 7's angr-6cp06 (its same-day memory calling it 'closed' was itself inaccurate, corrected here in round 8's memory on 2026-09-13 after bd's guard surfaced the discrepancy).

Testing PyO3 bridge logic in native/angr/src/claripy_bridge/ (export.rs, import.rs): the cargo-test env has NO Python interpreter and no claripy, so anything inside a Python::with_gil / call_method1 path is unreachable from cargo test. The established workaround is a PURE DECISION SEAM — lift the branch choice out of the Py-calling code into a small #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] enum plus an associated fn that takes only plain scalars, call it from the Py path, and unit-test the enum in the sibling *_tests.rs. Two instances now: ConcreteBvvEncoding::for_width (which BVV arg encoding a width takes, angr-ph300.52) and WidthFixup::decide(w0, w1, BoolCoercion) (how rustbv_to_claripy_memo reconciles a two-operand width mismatch, angr-c7xno.14). Since angr-5mnx3.11 the export-side seams live in their own file, export/width_decisions.rs (tests in export/width_decisions_tests.rs), whose module doc states the keep-pure rule: an item needing a py handle belongs in export/ast_helpers.rs instead. Reach for this before concluding a claripy_bridge branch 'can't be unit-tested'; it also documents the invariant as a named enum variant (e.g. WidthFixup::Reject) instead of an inline if. Companion rule from .14: in this module a fallback that papers over an upstream invariant violation must fail loud — ZeroExt-ing an unexplained narrower operand would silently sign-flip a signed op (Slt/SDiv), and RustBV's own width checks are debug_assert_eq! (compiled out in release), so the export path is the last line of defense, not a place to guess.

claripy_bridge/cache.rs has TWO thread_local caches with distinct roles (the file was claripy_bridge.rs before the zel8z.5 split; caches + tl_cache! macro + store/get/lookup/clear helpers now live in claripy_bridge/cache.rs). (1) AST_CACHE [LruCache<i64, RustBV>]: claripy→Rust, keyed by ast.hash() (stable across GC, unlike id(ast)); width-stale entries evicted on hit (cap 10000). (2) EXPRESSION_BY_OPERANDS_PTR [LruCache<usize, (RustBV, Py<PyAny>)>]: Rust→claripy for compound nodes keyed by Arc::as_ptr(operands); the RustBV in the value is LOAD-BEARING — pins the operands Arc alive to prevent allocator pointer reuse from causing wrong-AST returns. HISTORY: a third thread-local CLARIPY_AST_CACHE [HashMap<u64, Py<PyAny>>] (Rust→claripy for leaf symbols, keyed by rust_id) was REMOVED in angr-4xaga.2 (commit ac05abd92) — it duplicated SymbolicIdentityRegistry.rust_id_to_py exactly and could only 'hit' when the registry had already lost data it should not have. The Rust→claripy leaf-symbol AST mapping now lives SOLELY in the process-global SymbolicIdentityRegistry; store/get/evict_claripy_ast talk only to global_registry(). (The old hash-keyed EXPRESSION_CACHE was removed earlier, angr-fawo — see invariant-expression-cache-export-key.) WORKER-SAFETY SPLIT (angr-1ilq.2): both thread-locals are cleared by the worker-local clear_ast_cache() (used by RustExplorationManager.cleanup()); clear_worker_local_caches() is a self-documenting alias for the Option-A parallel scheduler to call on per-worker teardown — both touch ONLY this thread's caches. reset_for_new_exploration() (renamed from clear_all_caches in 1ilq.2) ALSO wipes the cross-thread global SymbolicIdentityRegistry; since angr-9ke6b.218 it is #[cfg(test)]-ONLY and deliberately so — no exploration start calls it, the registry survives across managers in one process on purpose (wiping it would strand rust ids live states still hold, angr-izov2). Cross-cache invariants now C1/C3/C4/C5 in claripy_bridge mod.rs rustdoc (C2/C6 removed with CLARIPY_AST_CACHE). NOTE (angr-0jh0j.10): these stale names kept resurfacing in prose — docs/advanced-topics/rust_engine.rst and RustExplorationManager.cleanup()'s docstring both still listed CLARIPY_AST_CACHE / clear_all_caches until 2026-08-16; grep both when this file changes again.

Counter doc comments rot in a specific, checkable way: a '/// Number of <fn> calls' doc is WRONG whenever the counter's fetch_add sits below an early return. Z3_BRANCH_CHECK_COUNT (symbolic/stats.rs) claimed 'Number of check_branch_feasibility calls' but bumps only after the concrete fast path returns, so it counts symbolic-condition calls; true total = it + Z3_BRANCH_CONCRETE_COUNT (the decomposition z3_saved_check_total in emit_solver_stats already used). Rule when auditing or adding a counter: read the increment SITE, not the function name, and if any early return precedes it, say which population the counter covers and name the sibling counter that completes the total. Companion to module-doc-scope-rot (angr-9ke6b.149, commit 044f8de5d).

Docs file-path citations drift across refactors just like bd-memory citations. TWO distinct failure modes, and the cheap check only catches the first:
(1) Path no longer exists — audit with: grep -rhoE '(native/angr/src|angr/exploration)[A-Za-z0-9_/.]+\.(rs|py)' docs/ | sort -u | while read f; do [ -e "$f" ] || echo MISSING: $f; done. Found+repaired 3 stale vex/ir.rs refs in rust_vex_ops.rst (file split into vex/ir/ in zel8z.7) in commit f766f6e7b. Caveat: a MISSING hit can be intentional (rust_engine.rst cites deleted spike lineage_assumptions.rs with its recovery commit) — verify context before editing.
(2) Path still exists but the SYMBOL moved out of it — invisible to (1) and to check_line_citations.py. This is the dominant mode around exploration/mod.rs, which repeated splits (manager_methods_* pymethods split angr-nbim4.1, event.rs/callback_types.rs extraction angr-zel8z.3) hollowed into a wiring module while docs kept citing it. Audit by resolving the SYMBOL, not the file: for each 'file.rs::sym' or 'file.rs:sym' in docs/, grep -rn 'fn sym|struct sym|enum sym' over the whole crate and compare the hit's file to the cited one. angr-c7xno.25/.31/.6 (commit 8db355b0c) fixed 12 such citations in one pass.
check_line_citations.py's baseline is CONTENT-keyed (file + the citing line's text), not line-numbered, so repairing a citation leaves a dead baseline entry behind — the gate still reports '0 new', it just quietly rots. Re-run with --update-baseline after any citation-repair sweep to prune them; that is a legitimate second use of the flag alongside the 'intentionally added a citation' case CLAUDE.md documents.
Complements [[refactor-memory-sweep-rule]].

emit_extract_z3_cached (value_z3.rs) cannot be deduped against RustBV::extract_into by delegating 'inner.extract_no_ctx(high,low).to_z3_ast_cached()': that INFINITE-LOOPS. extract_no_ctx returns a RustBV::Extract node for the default case; to_z3 of an Extract node re-enters build_z3_ast_cached's BVOp::Extract arm -> emit_extract_z3_cached with the SAME (inner,high,low) -> loop. RESOLVED in angr-ph300.81: the dedup uses value_ops::drive_extract driven by the ExtractTarget trait; ExtractTarget::recurse routes back through drive_extract (NOT to_z3 of a reconstructed node), and the Z3 default terminal applies z3 .extract() to the built inner AST directly. See extract-driver-unified. The concrete fold is also shared via bv_concrete::concrete_extract_u128 (moved from bv_codec into ungated symbolic/bv_concrete.rs in angr-1yge9.14 so it builds under --no-default-features; angr-ph300.36).

Rust-engine memoization caches must key on EVERYTHING the cached value depends on, not just the input expression. interpreter/concretize_cache.rs::bv_cache_key has now been the site of three separate wrong-answer bugs of exactly this shape: angr-owr37 (nested leaf identity dropped -> two distinct addresses collided), angr-9ke6b.89 (leaf variant untagged -> Concrete{value:N} vs Symbolic{id:N} collided), angr-360gt (producer CONFIG untagged -> a Multiple computed under read_range_limit=1024 was served to a store bound by write_range_limit=128, bypassing its Max fallback). The third is the subtle class: the key covered the input perfectly, but the cached value also depended on WHICH strategy chain produced it. Fix pattern: a namespace discriminant hashed into the key (see enum ConcretizeNs), not a post-hoc re-validation on hit — re-validation only works for shapes that carry their limit (TooLarge does; Multiple/Strided produced by the <=16 fast-enum path do not, since that path never consults the limit). When adding a new consumer to a shared cache, ask what config the entry was computed under; if it can differ, give it its own namespace.

INVARIANT (ccall guest-width truncation): a sub-64-bit guest's ccall flag helper computes in u64, so it MUST mask both its dep inputs and the arithmetic result to the guest width before extracting a flag bit. The dispatch site's RustBV::concrete(result, ret_bits) does NOT rescue an unmasked helper — it truncates 0x1FFFFFFFF to 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. turns garbage into different garbage instead of erroring. angr-03vl4.72: vex/ccall/arm32.rs::armg_calc_flag_n was the lone ARM32 per-flag helper without it, so ARMG_CC_OP_SUB with dep1=0,dep2=1 returned 0xFFFFFFFF for the N flag instead of 1, live on the standalone armg_calculate_flag_n CCall arm (taken whenever all four args are concrete). Its siblings armg_calc_flag_z/_c/_v mask on entry and mask each wrapping_* result; arm64 gets it for free via the shared arm64_res helper. When adding or reviewing a per-flag helper for a 32-bit guest, check BOTH masks — entry-only masking still lets a borrowing subtract sign-extend into the high half. Sibling rule: [invariant-ccall-flag-mask-named-constants].

RustBV::Concrete stores its value in a u128 (16 bytes / 128 bits max) regardless of declared width. Four hazard families follow. (1) ASSEMBLY: any code that ASSEMBLES a concrete value wider than 16 bytes by funneling bytes through a u128 is BUGGY: the shift wraps mod 128 in release (panics in debug), OR-ing high bytes back over low bytes. Fixed sites (commit df4bb4cd3, bd angr-tk7yv): memory/load.rs::load_concrete (two copies -- eager + lazy paths) now assemble size>16 loads as a Concat of per-byte concretes; symbolic/value_ops.rs::concat_into AND concat_no_ctx now guard the concrete-fold with 'if result_width <= 128' (else keep a Concat expression); exploration/state_api.rs::_get_state_memory reads in <=16-byte chunks. Also interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bytes_to_bv (angr-03vl4.31, commits 7608c8814 + 00b619214) -- the VEX-side twin of memory/load.rs::bytes_to_bv, reached from expressions.rs load fast paths, mod.rs read_memory and statements_dirty.rs::handle_dirty_call; it folds >16-byte inputs into a Concat via concat_no_ctx (high byte first: a.concat(b) puts a above b). Also interpreter/expressions.rs::eval_const's IRConst::V256 arm (angr-03vl4.29, commit 6ac725232) -- it packed v[0]|v[1]<<64 into ONE concrete tagged width 128, dropping v[2]/v[3]; now high.concat_no_ctx(&low) of the two 128-bit halves. Note the acceptance criteria said 'just retag the width as 256', which alone would have kept the truncation -- a wide width tag on a Concrete is a LIE, not a fix. Symptom seen: get_state_memory(24) on xmllint rodata returned chunk0|chunk2. Affects 32-byte AVX (ymm) concrete loads too. INVARIANT for future code: never pack >16 concrete bytes into a u128; build wide concretes via per-byte/per-chunk Concat, and do NOT 'fix' the overflow by clamping at 16 bytes -- that trades an abort for a silently truncated value. (2) BIT-SLICING (was invariant-concrete-extract-width128): bits at position >= 128 of a wider-than-128 Concrete (e.g. a 192-bit Multi-cell value) are logically zero, and RustBV::as_u128() returns Some for ANY Concrete width. Any bit-slicing on a concrete fast path (e.g. extract_into in symbolic/value_ops.rs) MUST guard BOTH: shift-by-low (v >> low overflows when low >= 128 -> result is 0) AND mask (1u128 << result_width overflows at result_width >= 128 -> use u128::MAX). Fixed in angr-dondi; mirrors the same width>=128 mask guard already in RustBV::concrete() (value.rs). (3) VEC-OP WIDENING (angr-sqfj8.118): adding 256-bit lane shapes to a vex/opcode_map*.rs parse arm (vector shapes live in opcode_map_vector.rs) silently makes that op's evaluator concrete fast path reachable at total_width=256, where 'result |= lane << lo' shifts a u128 by up to 192. Before widening ANY vector op family to V256, check its evaluator carries the 'if total_width <= 128' guard that vec_int_lane_op (ops/vec_int_lane.rs) has -- vec_shift_n (ops/vec_shift.rs; the merged shift-by-immediate helper that replaced vec_shl_n/vec_shr_n/vec_sar_n in angr-5mnx3.68) did not until .118. Applied again in angr-sqfj8.112 (V256 CmpEQ/CmpGT): vec_int_lane_op's existing guard is why that widening needed no evaluator change. The float lane ops were the last V256 op-coverage gap and are now covered too (angr-fs8kb.15, ops/tests_vec_float_lane.rs::test_vec_float_binops_avx2_256_bit_f32x8 and ::test_vec_float_min_max_sqrt_avx2_256_bit_f64x4); vec_float_lane_op's 'if total_width <= 128' guard was already present and correct. (4) SERIALIZATION (angr-03vl4.4): the reverse direction, RustBV -> bytes, has the mirror overflow ('value >> (i*8)' for i up to 31). interpreter/bv_utils.rs::bv_to_bytes stops at 16 bytes and zero-fills above, which IS correct there because as_u128() only ever exposes the low 128 bits -- but it means bv_to_bytes CANNOT serialize a wide Concat (as_u128() is None -> it returns all zeros); the reject_symbolic_byte_store guard is what keeps that from silently zeroing memory. callbacks/dispatch.rs used to carry a byte-identical private copy of bv_to_bytes that inherited every bug; it now imports interpreter::bv_utils::bv_to_bytes (which is pub(crate) for exactly that reason). Test pattern for a >128-bit op: build operands with concat_into of two 128-bit concretes and assert one extracted lane at a time (ops/tests_vec_int_lane.rs::test_vec_cmp_avx2_256_bit_i32x8); for the byte conversions see interpreter/bv_utils_tests.rs::bytes_to_bv_of_256_bit_buffer_keeps_every_byte_via_concat.

A code example that appears in BOTH a docs/*.rst worked example and a Rust module doc (//!) is one logical example with N copies, and a signature change reaches only the copy the author happened to be looking at. Concrete recurrence: angr-c7xno.64 fixed the stale 3-arg scan_for_null(state, addr, MAX_STRLEN) in simprocedures.rst -- and missed a SECOND copy 150 lines lower in the same file plus a third in procedures/macros.rs's module doc; both survived until angr-0jh0j.41/.39 two rounds later. RULE: when a shared helper's signature or dispatch changes, grep the helper/symbol name across docs/**/*.rst AND native/angr/src/**/*.rs doc comments -- not just the one file you are editing, and not just once per file (grep -n, count the hits, fix all of them). The line-citation gate (tools/check_line_citations.py) does NOT catch this class: a wrong argument list carries no line number. Same reasoning as refactor-memory-sweep-rule, applied to doc copies instead of bd memories.

automaton epsilon-closure cache contract (angr-9ke6b.193, 2026-08-03): EpsilonNFA::epsilon_closure (native/angr/src/automaton/epsilon_nfa.rs) now panics via a let-else with a descriptive message when a state id is >= the cached closure vec's length; it used to bounds-check-and-skip. Adds a THIRD tier to the assert-hardening rule of thumb from invariant-move-on-symbol-epsilon-result: (1) Result when PyO3-reachable with few callers, (2) debug_assert! for a pure-internal worklist invariant that would only mis-step, (3) unconditional panic! when skipping would produce a SILENTLY WRONG result in release builds — here a dropped state means a wrong closure means a wrong DFA, and debug_assert! alone would leave release builds silently wrong. epsilon_closure is pub but consumed only inside automaton:: (subset_construction + move_on_symbol + is_empty), so no PyO3 PanicException concern. The panic message names both causes (stale cache after a mutation that failed to clear epsilon_closures, or a caller-supplied non-state id) because both are bugs. Tested by epsilon_nfa_tests.rs::test_epsilon_closure_panics_on_stale_cache, which reaches into the private num_states field (tests are a child module via #[path]) to simulate the invalidation bug no public API can produce.

File-size split convention for native/angr/src (established angr-a2br.2 context.rs split, angr-7hwz value.rs split; test-file ambiguity resolved by angr-5mnx3.49 commit 5a84a60a0): every file — PROD AND TEST ALIKE — stays under ~2000 lines. Test files are NOT exempt; angr-p3bi's close text mused the owner 'may rule test files exempt' but the repo's actual shape had already settled the other way (vex/ops/tests_vec_*.rs, symbolic/value_ops_property_tests.rs, symbolic/value_z3_fp_tests.rs are all one-topic-per-file siblings). The split recipe, in order: (1) cut along the section banners already in the file — they are the author's own topic boundaries and land on test boundaries; (2) give each new file a //! module doc naming its scope and cross-referencing its siblings; (3) register each with test_submod!(z3 "file.rs" => modname) from the PROD file (keeping the same z3 gate — see no-default-features-test-gating), NOT from mod.rs; (4) a helper used by MORE THAN ONE resulting module moves to a shared <base>_tests_support.rs as pub(super) — sibling test modules are all children of the same prod module, so super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves; a helper used by exactly one stays private there. VERIFY the split lost nothing: grep -c the fn decls before and after (must match) and confirm cargo test --release reports the SAME pass count, not merely green. Then rename-sweep: moving a test between modules breaks doc citations of the form `module::test_name` — the value_tests split had 2 in-repo (value_ops_property_tests.rs) plus 7 bd memories to repair. PROD-side addendum (angr-5mnx3.1, arch/mod.rs -> register_file.rs + registry.rs): moving an `impl` block out of a mod.rs into a sibling breaks two things the type-checker only reports one at a time. (1) A method that was PRIVATE in the impl was visible to the `mod_tests.rs` sibling (both descendants of the same module); once the impl lives one level deeper it is not — widen exactly those to pub(super), not the whole impl. (2) An item that was DEFINED in mod.rs and is read only by tests (ArchDesc/ALL_ARCHES) becomes an `unused_imports` warning the moment it is re-exported instead, because the plain lib build has no consumer — CI clippy is --all-targets -D warnings, so it reds. Fix by making the sibling `pub(crate) mod` and having the tests path through it, keeping the re-export for the members lib code actually uses. (3) A type the moved code references ONLY in an intra-doc link (`[`SymContext`]` in a doc comment) must still be imported for rustdoc to resolve it, but rustc's unused_imports pass does NOT count doc-link uses — so the import warns and CI clippy -D warnings reds. Spell it `#[expect(unused_imports, reason = "referenced only by the intra-doc links below")]` rather than `allow`: if a later edit gives the import a real code use, unfulfilled_lint_expectations tells you to drop the attribute, whereas an `allow` would sit there forever. Seen in angr-fs8kb.35 (context.rs -> context_snapshot.rs / local_constraints.rs, both of which only name SymContext in prose). (4) angr-fs8kb.44 (sprintf.rs -> sprintf_spec.rs/sprintf_conv.rs, scanf.rs -> scanf_spec.rs): the `_tests.rs` sibling reaches the prod file's private items through `use super::*`, so ANY const/helper you move out of the prod file into a new sibling module breaks the test file even when the move is pure code motion and nothing changed visibility. rustc reports it as E0425 'cannot find value X in this scope' in the TEST file, pointing at the moved definition -- which reads like a visibility bug and is not; the fix is an explicit `use crate::<path>::<new_mod>::{X, y};` in the test file, plus pub(super) on the moved item. Corollary: do NOT keep the moved item imported in the prod file just to re-expose it to `super::*` -- with no lib-side consumer that is an unused_imports warning and CI clippy -D warnings reds, same trap as (2) above. (5) angr-fs8kb.20 (opcode_map.rs -> opcode_map_float.rs/opcode_map_vector.rs): when the prod file defines `macro_rules!` that the moved code invokes, textual macro scope does NOT follow the code to a SIBLING module (it covers only the defining module and its children), so each macro needs a `pub(super) use <name>;` line immediately after its definition and the new module imports it by path. Second half of the same trap: macro bodies name types unqualified (IROp/IRType/FCmpKind here) and macro_rules paths resolve at the CALL site, so the correct import list for each new module is whatever ITS OWN invocations expand to -- not a copy of the parent's `use` line. Expect the parent to shed an import as a result (FCmpKind became unused in opcode_map.rs once the fcmp_* invocations left), which CI clippy -D warnings will red. Verification for a macro-heavy split: grep -c the macro invocations (`_arms!`) as well as the fn decls before and after. (6) angr-fs8kb.66 (expressions.rs -> expressions_loads.rs/expressions_arith.rs): a baseline-gated audit script (tools/audit_silent_fallback.py and its four siblings) keys each known site by RELATIVE PATH, so moving a baselined line into a new file makes the gate report it as a NEW untagged site -- with the old entry now orphaned and silently unenforced. Fix by editing the one path in the baseline .txt (keeping its sorted position), NOT by --update-baseline, which would re-accept every other drift in the same run. Same reasoning as the pinned-baseline rule in run_regression.py: a refresh command hides the diff a hand edit makes reviewable. (7) angr-fs8kb.96 (statements_tests.rs -> statements_dirty_tests.rs/statements_cas_tests.rs): rule (4)'s `super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves` claim holds ONLY while every test module is registered from the SAME prod file. When the split is PER PROD SIBLING -- each test module registered from the file it covers, which is the shape rule (3) pushes you toward once the prod side is already split -- the consumers are children of DIFFERENT prod modules and no `super::` path reaches across them. Register the support module one level up, from the package's mod.rs, and have each test module import it by full crate path (`use crate::interpreter::statements_tests_support::{..};`). `pub(super)` on the helpers is still the right visibility: super is now the package module, so it scopes them to exactly the subtree that may use them, without widening to pub(crate). This is the one sanctioned exception to rule (3)'s register-from-the-prod-file-not-mod.rs -- and it applies to the SUPPORT module only; the test modules themselves still register from their own prod sibling.

Orphaned bd-memory citations in source comments are a live rot class (angr-9ke6b.36 found 5/8 dead in claripy_bridge/mod.rs; the repo-wide sweep found 13 more, tracked as angr-9ke6b.239). After Phase 1.1, an address byte in Rust SymbolicMemory can be in one of four states: (1) pure Concrete (no bitmap bits, no sidecar entries); (2) plain Symbolic (page.is_symbolic bit set, entry in symbolic_objects and/or symbolic_spans, NOT in multi_objects); (3) Multi (page.is_multi bit set, entry in multi_objects, NOT in symbolic_objects — set_multi_alternatives clears the symbolic entries); (4) inconsistent/transitional (any other combination, treated as a bug). The 'Multi supersedes Symbolic' rule is enforced by the set_multi_alternatives setter — see test_multi_supersedes_existing_symbolic in native/angr/src/memory/tests/multi/payload.rs. When transitioning a byte's state, clear the old sidecar entries before installing the new one. BOTH directions have a setter that does this and both MUST be used: Symbolic->Multi is `set_multi_alternatives`, Multi->Symbolic is `clear_multi_at` (drops the multi_objects payload AND the page multi_bitmap bit; safe no-op on a non-Multi byte). Note `MemoryPage::mark_symbolic` alone is NOT enough — it only touches symbolic_bitmap, so a path that marks a byte symbolic without `clear_multi_at` leaves state (4). This exact omission has now been found and fixed at every known Multi->Symbolic transition site, so treat any NEW one as guilty until it calls clear_multi_at: `SymbolicMemory::merge`'s collapse-a-Multi-side-into-an-ITE path (angr-0jh0j.31), `store_concrete`'s symbolic branch (angr-9ke6b.95), and `import_symbolic_value` (angr-6cp06.62 — the live flush_stores / flush_stores_to_rust_memory path, so it silently dropped ordinary symbolic stores at concretized addresses). The failure mode is identical in all three: load_concrete_common's range_has_multi check dispatches Multi-marked bytes to the Multi path BEFORE consulting symbolic_objects, and flush_multi_cells then writes the stale payload back over the new value on export. See also [[invariant-symbolic-byte-lane-lookup]] and [[invariant-every-load-path-gates-multi]].

invariant: a test whose whole assertion is 'nothing happened' (a defensive/no-op branch, an ignored ping, a guard that returns early) must be proven non-vacuous before commit — temporarily invert the input so the branch is NOT taken and confirm the test fails, then restore. Same reasoning as the valgrind/rounding-mode gates' --self-test (CLAUDE.md): an assertion that has never been seen to fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot. Worked example: exploration/scheduler_tests.rs::test_wake_worker_out_of_range_id_is_noop asserts PersistentPool::wake_worker with worker_id past job_txs' end emits no upstream WorkerUp within 250ms; swapping the out-of-range ids for 0 must (and does) fail the recv_timeout assert, because a woken worker re-parks and emits a second Quiesced. Without that step the timeout would also 'pass' if the pool were simply dead.

Before adding or trusting an IROp arm in native/angr/src/vex/opcode_map.rs or its opcode_map_float.rs / opcode_map_vector.rs siblings (angr-fs8kb.20 moved parse_float/parse_transcendental and parse_vector/parse_vreverse/parse_neon_unimplemented out of the parent), grep native/angr/vendor/pyvex_ffi.h for the exact Iop_ string — it is the vendored libVEX opcode enum and therefore the ground truth for what a real lift can emit. Two whole families were dead code that read as implemented coverage until angr-9ke6b.161/.162 (commit bad76646f): scalar Iop_MulHi{32,64}{S,U} (only vector Iop_MulHi<w>{U,S}x<n> exist; x86 IMUL/MUL lift to Iop_MullS32/Iop_MullU32 + Iop_64HIto32) and scalar Iop_Neg{8,16,32,64} (only float Iop_NegF32/Iop_NegF64 -> IROp::FNeg, the unmappable Iop_NegF128 -- IRType has no F128 variant -- and vector Iop_Neg32Fx2/Iop_Neg32Fx4/Iop_Neg64Fx2 exist; there is NO Iop_NegF16, so do not re-copy the old Iop_Neg{F16,F32,F64,F128} brace-enumeration this memory used to carry, corrected in angr-fs8kb.19; integer negation lifts as 0-x via Iop_Sub). The tell for this class: an opcode_map arm whose IROp variant has zero references in any *_tests*.rs — parse_opcode falls through to IROp::Unmapped for a name nobody emits, so the arm never fires and no test ever notices. The QDMulHi/QRDMulHi high-half vector family is genuinely unmapped (see invariant-qdmull-vex-op), which is a different thing from unreachable. The mirror-image shape also exists and is INTENTIONAL: an IROp variant that is fully implemented and tested but has no opcode_map producer because libVEX has no such opcode. IROp::ModS/ModU (no Iop_Mod* exists; guests use the combined Iop_DivMod*, and VEXOps::divmod_double_to_single takes its remainder straight from RustBV::urem/srem) and the bare 1-bit IROp::FCmp{EQ,LT,LE} (every real float compare carries a width/lane suffix -> FCmpScalarLane/FCmpVecPacked; suffix-free Iop_CmpF32/64 is the three-way FComCC and suffix-free Iop_CmpEQ8/16/32/64 are integer) are both documented as such at their ops_def.rs definition sites since angr-fs8kb.17/.18 — do not re-file them as dispatch gaps, and document any new one the same way.

Page bitmap is the AUTHORITATIVE source of truth for byte-level symbolic-vs-concrete state in SymbolicMemory, NOT symbolic_objects/symbolic_spans. The sidecar maps (symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects) are caches/indexes that can lag behind page-bitmap-driven state. store_concrete's page.store_concrete correctly clears the bitmap bits but does NOT clean wider-sym sidecar entries based at a different address. Any load fast path that returns a sym (or extract) without first verifying the bitmap is buggy. See bytes_all_marked_symbolic helper (memory/mod.rs angr-jvjf) for the bitmap consultation pattern.

COROLLARY for merge repair loops (angr-fs8kb.68). SymbolicMemory::merge's trailing adopt-from-other backfill iterates other.symbolic_objects keyed at each object's BASE address. Gating that repair on `Entry::Vacant` at the base key is wrong: OCCUPIED != RESOLVABLE. The both-present per-byte walk earlier in merge legitimately overwrites the base key with a fresh 8-BIT ITE, so for an object straddling a page boundary (base page both-present, tail page other-only) the Vacant test fails and the tail bytes' symbolic_spans inserts are skipped entirely — bitmap-symbolic with no sidecar resolving them, load errors out. Two generalizable rules: (1) the resolvability predicate is per byte, `SymbolicMemory::symbolic_byte_lane(...).is_some()`, never `map.contains_key(base)`; (2) you cannot repair by re-pointing symbolic_spans at the base — symbolic_byte_lane rejects a span whose recorded width disagrees with the base object's actual width — so install an 8-bit self-referential entry per byte, the same shape the both-present walk uses. Gate the repair on the bitmap (this memory) AND on the byte not being Multi (see [[invariant-multi-vs-symbolic-cell-states]]), or you manufacture the inconsistent fourth cell state. Behavioural coverage lives in memory/tests/merge_sidecars.rs; this is the third recurrence of the adopt-the-bitmap-forget-the-sidecar shape after angr-c7xno.50 (multi_objects) and angr-91vj9.3 (interior symbolic_spans).

PyO3 'multiple-pymethods' IS now enabled in this project (native/angr/Cargo.toml pyo3 features = [py-clone, abi3-py310, multiple-pymethods], angr-9ke6b.50). A pyclass may have MANY #[pymethods] impl blocks, in any module in the crate. RustExplorationManager's ~228-method surface is split across manager_methods.rs (construction/config/callbacks) + manager_methods_{hooks,state,constraints,procedures,techniques,export,run,stats}.rs, one #[pymethods] block each, all opened with 'use super::*;'. Two costs the flip carries, both handled: (1) it pulls in the 'inventory' crate (linker-section class registration) and pyo3 documents a compile-time cost; (2) SURPRISE -- see invariant-pyo3-multiple-pymethods-unmasks-unreachable-pub.

panic=abort makes any Python-supplied size a PROCESS-ABORT vector, not a catchable error. native/angr/Cargo.toml sets [profile.release] panic="abort", so nothing below is recoverable at the PyO3 boundary. Two shapes seen so far: (1) rangemap::RangeMap::{insert,remove} assert!(range.start < range.end), so an 'address..address + size' built from Python values without a checked_add guard aborts -- fixed in SegmentList::release (native/angr/src/segmentlist.rs, angr-9ke6b.199); SegmentList::occupy already had it. Convention: 'let Some(end) = address.checked_add(size) else { return; }' tagged // SILENT(cat-a), since a wrapping range describes no real region. (2) allocating a buffer whose length came straight from Python -- Vec's 'capacity overflow' panic near usize::MAX and handle_alloc_error for a merely huge size both abort. Fixed in Icicle::mem_read (native/angr/src/icicle.rs) via the free fn checked_read_len: reject a wrapping addr+size and a size above Icicle::max_mem_read_bytes (the mmu's own capacity()*page_size()), THEN allocate. Rule for new code: validate the range/length before you build it, whether the consumer is a RangeMap or the allocator; a free fn taking (addr, size, max) keeps it unit-testable where the surrounding type needs a VM/GIL.

Rustdoc intra-doc links in native/angr/src (updated angr-z3672, 2026-08-11). THREE authoring rules:
(1) A bare [`method_name`] never resolves — rustdoc only resolves names in *module* scope, so associated items need [`m`](Self::m) or [`Type::m`].
(2) An outer `///` doc comment on a `mod x;` DECLARATION makes rustdoc resolve *every* fragment of that module's docs — including the `//!` block inside x.rs — in the scope of the DECLARING module, not x's own. So `super::` shifts up one level and bare in-module item links break, silently, in a file you never touched. This was the root cause of 46 of the 100 warnings (run_loop_{single,steady,wave,worker} + scheduler, all declared with outer docs in exploration/mod.rs). Fix used: keep the module doc in the file's `//!` header and demote the declaration-site comment to plain `//`. Never pair an outer `///` on `mod x;` with a `//!` block in x.rs.
(3) Targets that can NEVER resolve under cargo doc — `#[cfg(test)]` items, `macro_rules!` names, items private-by-module — get a plain code span; never widen visibility just to make a doc link resolve. Note the *linking* item's visibility matters too: a `pub fn` doc linking to a private sibling trips `private_intra_doc_links` even though the target exists (5 of the angr-xtjm8 9: filesystem/ops.rs alloc_fd/offset_position, state/process.rs round_alloc_size). A pub(crate) linker with a pub(crate) target is fine. The crate-root `//!` block counts as public docs, so it may not link into pub(crate) modules at all.
GATE: --document-private-items is load-bearing (angr-sqfj8.144) — nearly every item here is pub(crate)/private, so without it rustdoc visits almost none of the docs and the lane passes with 83 broken links in the tree. Do not drop it.
LOCAL GATE (angr-z3672): the lane no longer lives only in CI. .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh runs the exact ci.yml command after clippy, under the same 'only when .rs files are dirty' guard — ~4.3s warm on the dev profile, ~0.3s when unchanged. That closes the regrowth loop this class kept riding (the box has no GitHub network, so CI never fires here). Do not remove it without replacing it in tools/ralph-gate.sh.
REFINEMENT of (3) re macro_rules! (angr-5mnx3.8): a `macro_rules!` name is resolvable by intra-doc links, but only TEXTUALLY AFTER its definition — callbacks/mod.rs has had [`with_callback_fields`] links resolving fine for months at sites below the macro_rules! block. Adding the same link to the file's `//!` module header (textually FIRST, before the definition) fails with 'exists in this crate, but it is not in scope at this link's location' — AND that one failure makes rustdoc re-report every other link to the same name, so a one-line doc edit can surface N errors at lines you never touched. Do not chase those; fix the out-of-scope one (demote it to a plain `code span!` per rule 3) and the rest go quiet.
SCOPE (angr-pr0tj, 2026-08-28): the gate is `cargo doc --workspace`, not `--manifest-path native/angr/Cargo.toml`. It was pinned at the latter in BOTH ci.yml's `Rustdoc link check` step and .claude/hooks/cargo-check-stop.sh, so the workspace's other member, native/angr-macros, was never documented and the pub `MergePolicy` derive's two links to the private VALID_MERGE_POLICIES / MECHANICAL_MERGE_POLICIES consts (a textbook rule-3 violation) sat red from the day it was written. Rules (1)-(3) apply to every member crate, not just native/angr/src. CI's clippy lane never had this hole — it runs from the repo root with no --manifest-path — and since angr-h3tx0 the Stop hook's clippy matches it. Keep any new gate command workspace-scoped so a member crate is covered on arrival. CARGO SUBTLETY the angr-h3tx0 measurement turned up: a --manifest-path-pinned clippy is NOT wholly blind to the other member — a workspace path dependency is not --cap-lints'ed, so angr-macros' *lib* was linted all along. What --manifest-path loses is --all-targets reach: only the pinned package's test/bench/example targets are selected, so a warning inside angr-macros' #[cfg(test)] mods, tests/compile_fail.rs or the trybuild ui harness scored 0 errors pinned and 2 workspace-wide. The same asymmetry does NOT hold for cargo doc, which never visits a dependency's docs at all — which is why the rustdoc half of this hole was total and the clippy half was partial.

Z3 interns constants BY NAME, so a symbolic BV's *name* is its identity in the solver — the Rust-side RustBV::Symbolic.id does NOT disambiguate. RustBV::from_parts (native/angr/src/symbolic/value.rs) lowers the name straight to z3::ast::BV::new_const, so any two RustBV::symbolic() calls that stringify the same name produce the SAME solver variable, even across unrelated states/contexts. Consequence: every fresh-symbol mint site must suffix a process-globally-unique token. Use SymContext::new_bv(base, width) (native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_id_ops.rs) — it appends next_id(), a process-global atomic, and mints exactly one id for both the name and the .id. A per-call or per-build local counter is NOT sufficient (angr-03vl4.41: SymbolicMemory::load_concrete_or_unconstrained and build_balanced_ite_load_after_prep both restarted at 0 per ITE-tree build, so the first unmapped leaf of two builds aliased). SymbolicMemory::unconstrained_read_value shows the other acceptable shape: a file-local process-wide AtomicU64. Grep for RustBV::symbolic( with a format! name when reviewing new code.

The USEFUL work on that allowlist is re-triage, not re-audit: a group whose reason says 'not yet implemented' may be stale because the op's evaluator is already lane-generic, making the widening a parse-table entry only. Why rustc's dead_code lint was blind in native/angr (angr-9ke6b.214, 2026-07-31): [lib] crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"] plus 23 'pub mod' declarations in lib.rs made every item externally-consumable, so dead_code reported 0 hits crate-wide while 468 unreachable_pub sites existed. Dropping rlib is impossible (benches/, examples/, tests/ and the fuzz/ cargo-fuzz project link it). The lever that works: keep rlib, but demote to 'pub(crate) mod' every top-level module no external target imports. Re-derive the keep-list with: grep -rhoE 'rustylib::[a-z_]+' native/angr/tests native/angr/benches native/angr/examples native/angr/fuzz | sort -u -- currently automaton, concretize, fuzz_api, memory, stash, state, symbolic, vex. After demoting, 'cargo clippy --fix --lib -- -W unreachable_pub' narrows the module-level items, and only THEN does dead_code fire. CRITICAL SECOND STEP: unreachable_pub does NOT lint methods inside inherent impl blocks, so 'pub fn' in 'impl Foo' stays invisible even in a pub(crate) module -- those 77 sites had to be narrowed by script, and doing so surfaced 11 MORE dead items (SegmentList::len/get_segment, PythonCallbacks::call_on_hook/call_on_syscall/call_get_register/call_put_register/get_inspect_enabled_for_debug, RustSolverContext::sym_context/from_sym_context_with_symbols). Exclude #[pymethods] impls from that pass -- PyO3 trampolines keep those live anyway. Other rustfix blind spots: items declared inside macro_rules! bodies (procedures/macros.rs, syscalls/support.rs stub_syscall!, syscalls/identity.rs constant_syscall!, interpreter/mod.rs define_execution_stats!) must be hand-edited; narrowing procedures::format_common::{parse_width_digits,parse_length_modifier,LengthModifier} breaks --features fuzzing with E0364/E0446 (they stay 'pub' with #[cfg_attr(not(feature="fuzzing"), allow(unreachable_pub))]). stat-family symlink semantics (angr-9ke6b.235, refined angr-zueuw): syscalls/file_path/stat.rs has two shared resolvers — stat_lookup_nofollow reports a FileSystem::readlink_target hit as st_mode=S_IFLNK_0777 sized to the raw target bytes, and stat_lookup_follow walks the symlink table up to MAX_SYMLINK_HOPS=8 then stats the final target; dangling link, non-UTF-8 target (targets are Vec<u8>, the known-path set is String-keyed) and cycles all return -1. Consumers: NativeLstatSyscall -> nofollow, NativeStatSyscall -> follow, NativeNewfstatatSyscall -> EITHER, selected by the AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW (0x100) bit of its flag arg. That flag branch is not optional polish: ARM64's asm-generic ABI dropped legacy lstat entirely (NativeLstatSyscall is registered only on AMD64/X86/ARM/MIPS32), so glibc lstat() on aarch64 lowers to fstatat(AT_FDCWD, path, buf, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and newfstatat is the ONLY no-follow stat entry point there — any future stat-family handler that takes an AT_* flag must decide follow-vs-nofollow from it, and must treat a symbolic flag as SymbolicArgument (defer to Python) rather than assuming follow, since the two branches report different st_mode. write_stat_for_arch and all five per-arch writers take st_mode as a parameter — do NOT reintroduce a hardcoded S_IFREG_0755 inside a writer. MIPS32 is the one arch where a symlink is invisible to lstat: write_mips32_stat mirrors angr's _store_mips32, which emits NO st_mode field, so it takes _mode and only st_size differs. See symlink-table-readlink-model for the table itself.

Scheduler serde-budget gate makes offload tests pass VACUOUSLY: any Rust unit test that calls exploration::scheduler_worker::offload_surplus MORE THAN ONCE over the same SchedulerCounters must preset counters.step_ns (e.g. u64::MAX/8). The first call's detach_timed charges serde_ns, and offload_is_affordable is serde*SERDE_BUDGET_DIVISOR <= step — with the default step_ns==0 the budget shuts Trigger A off for every later call, so the test asserts 'nothing was offloaded' for the wrong reason. Caught by mutation-check during angr-fs8kb.5 (test_trigger_a_nets_out_states_already_queued_for_idle_siblings): the pre-fix semantics PASSED the test until step_ns was preset. Corollary of the general rule — always mutation-check a scheduler test, because the budget gate is a second, invisible reason for a zero-offload outcome.

claripy AST __hash__ is content-addressed and STABLE for a given AST object across CPython gc (verified empirically: hash(x) unchanged after gc.collect()). This is why claripy_bridge::cache's AST_CACHE is keyed by ast.hash() rather than id(ast), which CPython can recycle after collection. Two DISTINCT ASTs denoting the same symbol legitimately hash differently (annotations, BVS explicit_name suffixes) — that is what symbolic::registry::update_hash_mapping exists for, not hash mutation. A former claripy_bridge::get_stable_ast_id helper documented the opposite ('hash changes due to garbage collection or object reallocation') and preferred ast._hash over __hash__(); it was deleted in caf870723 (angr-9ke6b.214). Note ast._hash != hash(ast) in claripy 9.2.209, so resurrecting that preference would silently desync from the AST_CACHE key. Cross-cache invariant C5's width check lives in the AST_CACHE hit arm of claripy_bridge::import::claripy_to_rustbv_depth.

Iop_CasCmpEQ/CasCmpNE 8/16/32/64 were missing from the STRING path of opcode_map.rs::parse_comparison despite being correctly mapped in parse_opcode_from_u32 (0x1431-0x1438, comment 'same as CmpEQ/CmpNE'). pyvex's string-based lifting (which the angr Rust engine uses) silently dropped them via the IROp::Raw(0) fallback, causing cmpxchg/cmpxchg16b blocks to produce fresh-symbolic zeros that test_dcas_cmpxchg16b_no_match_keeps_memory was just-barely tolerating. This regression only surfaced when angr-tkbr.2 (commit 8b9ff2713) replaced the silent Raw(0) path with a hard typed error. Fix: add tuple_arms! mappings for CasCmpEQ/CasCmpNE in parse_comparison so they route to IROp::CmpEQ/CmpNE. Other ops likely have similar string-vs-integer-path gaps; when adding to parse_opcode_from_u32, mirror in parse_*. ADDENDUM (2026-08-03, iter163): parse_opcode_from_u32 and the whole numeric/FFI opcode path NO LONGER EXIST -- opcode_map.rs is string-only now (entry point parse_opcode, dispatching to parse_arithmetic/bitwise/shift/comparison/conversion/float/vector/vreverse/special/neon_unimplemented). Unmapped names now log::warn! and return IROp::Unmapped(intern_unmapped_op(op_str)), which dispatch turns into a typed UnsupportedVexOp error (no silent Raw(0)). So the 'mirror the numeric path' advice is moot; the live analogue is that a family can still be PARTIALLY mapped. Related invariant: the tuple_arms!/vec_arms!/scalar_arms! macros match the suffix EXACTLY (strip_prefix + literal match arm), so a suffixed sibling like Iop_ClzNat32 can never be silently mistaken for Iop_Clz32 -- it falls through to Unmapped and defers loudly. Known deliberate family gaps carry an 'unmapped for now'-style comment: Iop_CmpORD* in parse_comparison, and Iop_ClzNat/CtzNat in the parse_conversion catch-all arm (absent from vendor/pyvex_ffi.h on the current VEX pin; map them when the pin is bumped).

Rust ccall rflags_c/eflags_c symbolic-carry path (handle_x86_eflags_c in native/angr/src/vex/ccall/mod.rs, reached from handle_ccall_with_ctx's name dispatch — it was inline in handle_ccall_with_ctx before the angr-5mnx3.60 helper split) must cover ALL OpCategory variants, not just Copy/Sub/Add/Logic. INC/DEC do NOT modify CF — VEX preserves it in cc_ndep (args[3]); the carry is CF=(cc_ndep>>G_CC_SHIFT_C)&1 (SHIFT_C==0), same formula as concrete calc_flags_inc/calc_flags_dec. angr-g6dg root cause: the rflags_c symbolic match had Inc/Dec in the '_ => None' arm, so when cc_dep1/cc_ndep were symbolic (cold blank_state blob, dec preserving carry) the whole ccall returned None and eval_ccall (expressions_arith.rs) substituted a FRESH unconstrained symbolic carry, poisoning flags threaded into later loop iterations. NOTE: a jnz/jz loop guard is often compiled by VEX to a direct CmpEQ32(result,0) (NO condition ccall), so a ZF-based countdown loop does NOT exercise this bug — you need a CF-dependent path (jc/jb/jae) or the carry-preservation chain through consecutive dec/inc. Fixed commit f761d0493 (Inc|Dec arms added). When adding cc_op categories, mirror both the concrete calc_flags_* and the symbolic SymFlags builder.

Two gotchas: (1) the label is passed EXPLICITLY, not derived from op_str, because several arms match two claripy op-names and report a canonical one whose spelling differs from both ('div' for SDiv, 'mod' for SMod) -- do not 'simplify' it to op_str, that silently changes error text; (2) 'RustBV::eq' / 'RustBV::ne' as fn-pointer paths resolve to the INHERENT 3-arg ops in symbolic/value_ops.rs, not PartialEq::eq (RustBV does impl PartialEq at value.rs) -- it compiles because the signatures disagree, but keep that in mind if the inherent ops are ever renamed. Unary/variadic/index-carrying arms (__neg__, __invert__, ZeroExt, SignExt, Extract, Concat, If, And, Or, Not, Reverse) deliberately stay hand-written.

DCAS (interpreter/statements_cas.rs::execute_cas_stmt — file is statements_cas.rs, NOT statements.rs) explicitly rejects big-endian endness with CbExecutionError::Unsupported(format!("{DCAS_UNSUPPORTED_REASON} with big-endian memory not supported")) — since angr-fs8kb.59 the message is built from the marker const so the manager's dcas_unsupported_count and per-state warning actually fire (before that the hand-written text omitted the marker and the counter was permanently dead; the same invariant now heads execution_error.rs's module doc for every reason-marker const). Since angr-inieg.2 the CAS operands arrive bundled as a CasArgs struct (endness is CasArgs::endness), and cas_load_dcas_high reads expdHi/dataHi off it rather than taking them pre-unwrapped — the all-Some/all-None DCAS gate still lives in execute_cas_stmt. declare_proc! macro at native/angr/src/procedures/macros.rs lets new SimProcedures be added with one args list driving name(), num_args(), and extraction (no manual impl block). Two arg kinds: 'concrete' (extracts u64; symbolic falls back to Python) and 'bv' (clones the raw RustBV; body decides handling). Optional 'no_return = true' flag. DFA::minimize (native/angr/src/automaton/dfa.rs) uses a NON-textbook Hopcroft worklist: entries are (partition_INDEX, symbol), not (partition_set, symbol). On a split the LARGER half keeps the old index -- silently inheriting every still-pending entry that named it -- and only the smaller half is enqueued under a fresh index. Soundness argument (an in-code comment above the worklist decl): determinism means a state has at most one s-successor, so pred(keep,s) and pred(add,s) are DISJOINT and their union is pred(Y,s); the inherited entry plus the fresh one together separate every pair the original splitter would have. That index invariant is now enforced by a debug_assert! at the dequeue site (angr-9ke6b.182 replaced an unreachable 'else { continue }' that would have silently dropped a splitter). NOTE: debug_assert! is compiled OUT of 'cargo test --release', which is what the ralph gate runs -- to actually exercise it use 'cargo test --manifest-path native/angr/Cargo.toml --lib automaton' (debug profile). NOT textbook Hopcroft and NO O(n*|Sigma|*log n) bound (angr-9ke6b.184): both initial partitions are seeded (not only the smaller), there is no in-worklist membership tracking, and each popped splitter rescans EVERY partition instead of only pred-touched ones; docs now say 'Hopcroft-style partition refinement' everywhere. Regression coverage in dfa_tests.rs: test_minimize_splits_pending_splitter (hand-traced 7-state case where 1 and 2 are told apart only by the inherited entry) and test_minimize_matches_moore_reference (400 LCG-seeded complete 2-symbol DFAs vs an independent table-filling reference, comparing class count AND language). TRAP found while writing these: minimize() does NOT return the empty DFA for a language-empty input that still has reachable states -- it returns the single non-final class (1 state), which is what Moore reports too; only start_state=None / num_states=0 / no reachable states take the DFA::new() early return. Language-preservation helpers accepts/words_up_to/assert_same_language live in dfa_tests.rs and are reusable for any automaton test.

Z3 has no fpa_min / fpa_max op (only fpa_add/sub/mul/div/sqrt/neg/abs/fma + cmp/eq/lt/leq). A step counts when cancel is set on process() return but the step did NOT itself raise it (!request_cancel) — i.e. an in-flight step committed before a peer's find-cancel became visible. WASTE TABLE (RUST_PARALLEL_STEADY=1): fork_solve_W6_S8 W6 -> 5/9 tasks = 55.6%; xmllint_getenv W6 -> 0/23; ais3_crackme W4/W8 -> 1/98 = 1.0%; csaw_wyvern W8 -> 0/33; fauxware W4 -> 0/18; defcamp_r100 W4 -> 0/15. Native MergePoint technique (angr-op0dn.11.5, ManualMergepoint parity): NativeTechnique::MergePoint { address, wait_counter_limit, counter, wait_stash } in native_technique.rs; registered via register_merge_point pymethod (manager_methods_techniques.rs, creates per-address merge_waiting_{addr:#x} stash). register_merge_point is IDEMPOTENT PER ADDRESS since angr-fs8kb.2: a second call for an address that already has a MergePoint updates that entry's wait_counter_limit in place (last call wins, log::warn when the value changes) and resets its counter -- do NOT restore the unconditional push, because two entries share the address-derived wait stash and the first entry's apply_merge_point drains it every round, so the second always sees wait_len==0 and returns above its own counter tick (permanently dead, wait_counter silently ignored). Applied post-round in apply_native_techniques (native_technique.rs) but HANDLED OUT OF BAND above the match: merging calls _merge_states (needs &mut self) which conflicts with the &mut self.native_techniques[tech_idx] the match arm holds -- caller copies immutable fields out first, writes counter back via short reborrows keyed by tech_idx. apply_merge_point: park_states_at_address moves active states with pc==address to wait stash (fresh arrival resets counter to 0); once active drains OR wait_counter_limit post-step rounds elapse, merge_waiters_by_callstack groups waiters by call_stack return_addr chain (first-appearance order for determinism), merges each >=2 group via _merge_states (forks+pushes merged to active, bumps states_merged_native; sources dropped via drop_states_by_id), lone-callstack waiters released to active unmerged. IMPORTANT: _merge_states does NOT consume sources (it forks), so the technique must drop them. Python: rust_techniques.py routes ManualMergepoint->register_merge_point and 'ManualMergepoint' is in _NATIVE_STEP_TECH_NAMES so its Python step() hook is suppressed (no double-merge). Native serial loop applies techniques after EACH single-state step (not per full round), so counter ticks faster than Python's per-step()-of-whole-stash; primary merge trigger is active-empty, counter is the fallback. Uses RustSimState::push_call in tests (not push_call_frame -- that's a pymethod).

sprintf/printf int narrowing (angr-n0irt.4): native sprintf.rs must mask each concretized int arg to the length-modifier's width before formatting, mirroring format_parser.py:96 c_val&=(1<<size*8)-1. Widths: hh=8, h=16, none=32, l/ll/z/j/t=64 -- use int_conv_bits(modifier)+signed_at_width/unsigned_at_width helpers in sprintf_conv.rs, do NOT special-case only long/long_long. CONFIRMED root cause (angr-duav3): native NativeStrnlen does NOT defer due to any strnlen-specific defect. It is never ATTEMPTED in the TestSymbolicLibcProcedures harness because that harness deliberately hooks at an IN-BINARY address (HOOK_ADDR=0x4008C0, fauxware .fini area) so RustExplorationManager._run_python_init_if_needed short-circuits (an out-of-binary PC instead triggers full Python init-to-main, running the whole binary). BOTH native dispatch sites (run_loop.rs handle around line 244-251, stepping.rs handle_simprocedure is_in_binary check ~line 749-756) skip native procs whenever the hook addr is inside environment.binary_regions, treating them as user-placed hooks where the explicit Python SimProcedure must run. So in the harness: is_in_binary=true -> native skipped entirely (no native_proc_stats bucket touched, the else->None branch) -> Python strnlen runs -> returns full strlen=8 (ignores maxlen). The simprocedure_fallback_by_name={'strnlen':1} from iter-14 is the FINAL Python-fallback counter (run_loop.rs ~line 382) which fires for ALL in-binary hooks. Native strnlen DOES run for real external/PLT-resolved calls (is_in_binary=false), like strcmp/read/puts do during normal fauxware execution. NOT a bug, NOT a divergence. Repro: hook strnlen at 0x4008C0 vs 0x900000 -> 0x4008C0 gives rax=8 no native attempt; 0x900000 runs full binary via init-short-circuit.
