Any 'zero production callers' claim about a method on `Arch` / `CallingConvention` / any other trait must be re-derived by grep, not inferred from a clean clippy run. Worked example: Arch::register_name (angr-9ke6b.8) truly has no non-test caller and clippy --all-targets -D warnings is still clean. Decision rule when such a method turns up: (1) DELETE if it returns a hardcoded/guessed answer that would be wrong for its first real caller (precedent: CallingConvention::endness, angr-9ke6b.218 item 7); (2) DELETE if it duplicates logic that already exists elsewhere with its own tests, even when the copy is correct — the tests only pin the dead copy, so the live one can silently diverge (precedent: CallingConvention::extract_args, angr-9iny6: deleted along with its 3 tests and the MemoryUnavailable variant only it produced, because exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi is the real path and helpers_tests.rs already pins every branch); (3) KEEP + document if it is a correct computation whose only callers are load-bearing invariant tests that would lose real coverage (precedent: Arch::register_name, whose deletion would take out mod_tests::exported_register_names_reverse_resolve, ..::register_names_all_resolve_and_fit_in_u128, ..::vex_bookkeeping_fields_resolve_on_every_arch and two calling_conventions_tests sweeps; also CallingConvention::fp_arg_registers, whose per-ABI tables carry provenance FP-arg support will need).

Deciding whether a VEX opcode actually exists on this pin needs TWO sources, and one grep shape lies. (1) The IROp enum in native/angr/vendor/pyvex_ffi.h (lines ~159-708, Iop_INVALID..Iop_LAST) is the complete enum for the pin. (2) strings .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/pyvex/lib/libpyvex.so, matched ANCHORED (grep -xE 'Clz(8|16|32|64)') -- these are the ppIROp name strings pyvex hands us, so they are what opcode_map.rs actually sees.

TRAP that cost a wrong conclusion at iter164: grep -oE 'Iop_Clz[0-9]+' on the header reports Iop_Clz8/Clz16 -- but those are prefix hits on the NEON lane ops Iop_Clz8x8 / Iop_Clz16x4 / Iop_Clz8x16. Scalar Clz/Ctz really is only 32/64 (header line ~177). Always anchor the width or exclude the 'x' lane suffix.

Findings for the current pin (angr-9ke6b.166): Iop_Not1 exists but Iop_And1/Or1/Xor1 do NOT; there is NO scalar PopCount at any width (x86 POPCNT lifts to the gen_POPCOUNT dirty helper, not an IROp); ClzNat/CtzNat do not exist either (angr-9ke6b.167).

POLICY settled on both beads: a map arm for a nonexistent opcode is DOCUMENTED, not deleted. tuple_arms!/vec_arms!/scalar_arms! strip_prefix then match the suffix EXACTLY, so a dead arm costs one failed compare and can never misfire onto a real opcode; and for PopCount the evaluator (popcount_into via VEXOps::unop) plus unit tests already exist, so deleting only the parse arm would strand a working impl with no route in. See parse_bitwise and the parse_conversion '_ =>' fallback in native/angr/src/vex/opcode_map.rs.

vex vector-IROp drift guard: vex/ops/tests_vec_dispatch.rs (test_vec_int_binops_iropclass_is_vec + test_vec_int_binops_dispatch_reachable) pins the 3 hand-maintained lists (iropclass in vex/ops/classify.rs; the binop() router vec-int arm and binop_vec_int arms, both in vex/ops/mod.rs). Paths updated for the angr-9ke6b.170/.171 ops/ split — the old flat vex/ops.rs and ops_tests_vec_dispatch.rs are gone. Key insight: iropclass() is a compile-time-EXHAUSTIVE match (no wildcard _), so a new IROp variant CANNOT be silently unclassified — the compiler forces classification. The real residual drift is (a) MIS-classification (wrong family) and (b) router<->binop_vec_int mismatch, where a dropped/added arm falls to '_ => Err(NotBinary)' in binop_vec_int or binop_misc and silently defers to Python. The dispatch test asserts !NotBinary for the V128/V128 (+V128/i8) subset; width-heterogeneous ops (VMull/VNarrowBin/VQNarrowBin) covered by their dedicated vex/ops/tests_vec_* files. When adding a V* integer binop, add it to vec_int_binops() so both tests cover it. ADDENDUM (angr-9ke6b.168, 2026-08-03): dispatch grouping and family grouping are INDEPENDENT axes and are allowed to disagree — dispatch tracks code shape, iropclass tracks semantics. Canonical case: IROp::Concat is dispatched to binop_vec_int (two-narrow-in/one-wide-out matches the vector-int helpers) but classified VexOpFamily::Ext next to Extract/SignExtend (it is a width adjustment, not SIMD). Both sites now carry cross-reference comments. So when adding an op, pick the 'nearest example' in each grouping independently; do not infer one from the other.

add_constraints_ast (native/angr/src/solver.rs; named add_constraints before the angr-sqfj8.124 rename) partial-batch contract: the raw Z3-AST fast path converts entries until one AST fails the is_bool() / claripy_to_rustbv gate, then flushes the converted PREFIX via SymContext::add_constraints_raw_batch and resumes from the failing index with per-constraint add_constraint_ast. Two invariants any future edit must keep: (1) resume_from == entries.len(), so a failure at index 0 means an EMPTY batch (add_constraints_raw_batch early-returns on empty) and resume_from=0 -- off-by-one here silently DROPS a constraint; (2) prefix-then-remainder preserves the original constraint order, which the unbatched loop guaranteed. Measured on N=300 Bool + 1 non-Bool last entry: pre-fix 4.406ms, post-fix 3.595ms (-18%), identical to a batch with no failure at all. Regression-covered by test_add_constraints_ast_mixed_batch_applies_every_entry and test_add_constraints_ast_leading_failure_still_applies_rest in tests/engines/rust/test_solver_ops.py. (angr-9ke6b.206)

arch_from_name (native/angr/src/arch/registry.rs) accepted names must all resolve to a CallingConvention. Since angr-9ke6b.216 both sides read ONE table: ALL_ARCHES (arch/registry.rs), a const slice of ArchDesc { name, aliases, vex, make_arch, make_cc }; arch_from_name/arch_from_vex/cc_for_arch/default_cc_for_arch all iterate it via arch_desc_from_name, so the completeness invariant is structural rather than a coincidence between two hand-written lists. Before that, arch_from_name had match arms and each CC carried its own ARCH_ALIASES const, which drifted. RustExplorationManager::new (manager_methods.rs) calls arch_from_name THEN default_cc_for_arch on the same string; a name accepted by the former but missing a CC passes the lookup then PANICS in default_cc_for_arch (PanicException) — a recognized alias failing more violently than an unrecognized one (clean PyValueError). test_arch_from_name_names_all_have_a_cc pins completeness; test_arch_aliases_disjoint pins no-overlap. To add an alias, add it to the ALL_ARCHES row.

ALL_ARCHES (native/angr/src/arch/registry.rs) name+aliases spellings must stay disjoint across rows. arch_desc_from_name walks the table in declaration order, so a spelling in two rows makes both arch_from_name and default_cc_for_arch silently order-dependent. test_arch_aliases_disjoint (arch/calling_conventions_tests.rs) pins this; do not weaken it. Superseded the per-CC ARCH_ALIASES consts deleted in angr-9ke6b.216. Decision recorded there: 'mips64be' is deliberately NOT a registered name — MIPS64 big-endian states are built as 'mips64' + Iend_BE; it used to sit in MipsN64::ARCH_ALIASES while arch_from_name rejected it, and the merge resolved that by rejecting it everywhere (test_mips64be_is_not_a_registered_arch_name).

The architecture-independent register spellings in native/angr/src/arch/*.rs ALIASES tables are "sp", "bp" (angr-6qzik) and "pc" (angr-9ke6b.217) — all six arches now resolve all three. There is deliberately NO "ip" alias on ANY arch: on ARM the ABI calls r12 "ip", so exposing the ABI reading made a Python write through "ip" land in r12 instead of the PC (angr-itm3u). RustStateProxy._canonical_name rewrites "pc"/"ip" to the arch canonical name via archinfo before the name reaches Rust, so the Python path never depended on these; they exist for direct Rust-level / RustSimState.set_register callers. Gate: arch/registry_tests.rs::test_all_arches_report_expected_special_register_offsets asserts register_offset("pc") == ip_offset on every ALL_ARCHES row. NOTE tests/engines/rust/test_arch_offset_parity.py CANNOT catch a missing alias — its harness skips any archinfo name Rust does not know, so absent names are invisible there; only the Rust sweep sees them.

native/angr/src/interpreter/concretize_cache.rs::bv_cache_key routes EVERY RustBV variant through hash_bv (angr-9ke6b.89) — it does not shortcut Concrete to *value or Symbolic/Constrained to *id, and each arm hashes its FULL payload (angr-fs8kb.65). Rationale: untagged leaf shortcuts made Concrete{value:N} and Symbolic{id:N} share a u64 key. INVARIANT 1: keep the single hash_bv path — do not reintroduce a 'cheap' leaf shortcut for perf; the symbolic-leaf hash is a few ns against a Z3 concretize call and the bench gate showed no movement (22/22, 31.2s). INVARIANT 2 (the trap this function fell into twice): the 'all three call sites early-return on addr.as_u64(), so Concrete/Constrained can never reach here' argument scopes ONLY to the TOP-LEVEL value. hash_bv recurses into Expression operands, where those variants are routine — angr-owr37 dropped nested leaf identity by hashing 1 level, and angr-fs8kb.65 dropped Constrained's 'value' field under exactly that call-site justification, making Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:10}) and Add(y,Constrained{id:5,value:20}) hash byte-identically (a guaranteed, not probabilistic, collision). Generalize: a call-site precondition NEVER justifies dropping a field from a RECURSIVE hash/key function. Regression tests: concretize_cache_tests.rs::bv_cache_key_distinguishes_leaf_variants_with_equal_scalars (top-level) and ::bv_cache_key_distinguishes_nested_constrained_values (nested).

All six x86/amd64 concrete ccall flag builders that take RAW operands — calc_flags_add, calc_flags_sub, calc_flags_adc, calc_flags_sbb, calc_flags_umul, calc_flags_smul (native/angr/src/vex/ccall/x86_concrete.rs) — now mask their operands to get_mask(nbits) BEFORE use, matching the symbolic siblings in x86_symbolic.rs which extract_to_nbits unconditionally. Add/sub got this under angr-36vvn.3; umul/smul under angr-0jh0j.69 (umul's hi = (prod >> nbits) & mask picked up cross-term corruption from garbage above the width, wrecking CF/OF; sign_extend_to_i64's non-negative branch returned val verbatim so nbits=8 val=0x100 multiplied as 256 instead of 0). SUPERSEDES the old claim that calc_flags_sub/add compare on raw u64 — they no longer do, and a diff-fuzz no longer needs to pre-mask to agree (the memory key still says 'unmasked' only so existing citations keep resolving). ccall_tests.rs::diff_fuzz_sym_flags_unmasked_inputs is the gate: it diffs concrete vs symbolic over Add/Sub/Adc/Sbb/Logic/Umul/Smul with UNMASKED random operands and also pins that masking the inputs changes nothing. When adding a new concrete flag builder that takes raw operands, mask first and extend that test's category list — every other diff_fuzz_sym_flags_* pre-masks and cannot see this bug class.

PythonCallbacks (native/angr/src/callbacks/mod.rs) has ONE source of truth for its Option<Py<PyAny>> callback slots: the with_callback_fields! macro, which expands to $m!{field, field, ...}. new(), traverse_fields and clear_fields are all generated from it via local macro_rules! consumers (empty_holder / visit_fields / clear_all), and since angr-0jh0j.6 so is every set_<slot> PyO3 setter, via the angr_macros::callback_setters! proc macro (driven as `with_callback_fields!(callback_setters PythonCallbacks =>)`; it emits its OWN #[pymethods] impl block because an attribute proc macro cannot see through an unexpanded macro_rules! invocation inside one). So adding a callback is exactly TWO places: the struct definition (doc comment + type) and that list -- the Python-visible setter follows for free. Per-slot prose (expected Python signature, degraded paths, confusable siblings) belongs on the struct FIELD's doc comment, which the generated setter doc links to. WHY it matters: traverse_fields and clear_fields back __traverse__/__clear__ on BOTH PythonCallbacks and RustExplorationManager (which holds a clone). A slot present in one list but not the other, or missing from both, silently keeps the mgr -> _callbacks -> bound method -> mgr reference cycle alive and leaks the manager plus its _state_cache (~4030 angr pages/call on mma_howtouse -- the 9maq leak). ENFORCEMENT is compile-time, not a test: clear_fields destructures 'let Self { ... } = self' EXHAUSTIVELY, deliberately without a '..' rest pattern, so a field added to the struct but not the list has no binding and fails to build. Do NOT 'fix' that by adding '..' -- that silently disarms the guard. Self-tested (angr-9ke6b.27) by adding a probe field to the struct alone: E0063 from the new() expansion + 'pattern requires .. due to inaccessible fields' from the clear destructure. The non-Py Arc fields (inspect_enabled, memory_is_rust_proxy, python_servable_pages, python_page_universe) are named explicitly in the destructure (three as ': _') for the same reason. Runtime half pinned by callbacks_tests.rs::clear_fields_drops_every_callback_slot. [Deliberately states NO slot count: an earlier revision of this memory cited '34' against an actual 30 -- a live instance of the cardinality-drift anti-pattern this convention warns about elsewhere (lane_traits.rs / CLAUDE.md). Cite the with_callback_fields! list by name, never by count.]

Phase 4.2 flush_multi_cells (multi.rs::flush_multi_cells) coalesces runs of adjacent Multi bytes ONLY when payload_cond_fingerprint() matches across consecutive addresses. For RustBV::Expression the fingerprint mixes Arc::as_ptr identity of the operands with a hash of the BVOp (angr-03vl4.38); the pointer half relies on install_multi_for_candidates building one cond RustBV per candidate then cloning into each byte (so neighbours from the same store-call share the same Arc), and on value_ops::expr_node allocating a fresh operands Arc per node. Any new store path that emits Multi bytes MUST follow this 'build cond once, clone into each byte' pattern, or it will silently fall back to the per-byte flush path (correctness preserved, perf loss). Run length is capped at COALESCE_MAX_RUN=16 because RustBV::concat_into's u128 concrete fast-path silently truncates widths >120+8. Lift the cap only after auditing concat_into for wider-than-128 safety.

RustBV concrete fast-paths that shift/mask a u128 by a bit position (not an operand-supplied amount) must guard for width>128: a Concrete stores its value in a u128, so any bit >=128 is logically zero, and shifting a u128 by >=128 is a debug abort / release mod-128 wrap. Canonical guards live in extract_into (value_ops.rs): shift=0 when low>=128, mask=u128::MAX when result_width>=128; concat_into keeps result_width>128 as a Concat expr instead of folding. extract_no_ctx had the same window logic but WITHOUT the guards until angr-ph300.31 -> aborted/mis-extracted on 256-bit ymm sub-register overlays (arch/register_file.rs extract_no_ctx callers). Any new concrete BV op that shifts by a bit position must copy extract_into's guards. Complements [[invariant-concrete-shift-clamp-before-narrow]] which covers operand-amount narrowing.

The interpreter's per-block `concretize_cache` (interpreter/concretize_cache.rs, cleared at the top of execution.rs::execute_block_with_callbacks) is SHARED by three entry points with three different strategy chains — concretize_cached_read (Range(read_range_limit) -> Any), concretize_cached_write (Range(write_range_limit) -> Max, or Max-only when SYMBOLIC_WRITE_ADDRESSES is off), and concretize_cached_jump (plain AddressConcretizer::concretize = read-limit chain, NO fallback; added angr-9ke6b.92 for exits.rs::eval_next_addr). Sharing one map across mismatched chains is sound for the Single case for a non-obvious reason: every fallback Single is produced via concretize::pin_fallback_addr, which does ctx.assume_true(addr == chosen) — a REAL solver constraint, not a local pick. So once any variant has cached a fallback Single, a fresh concretize on the same expression is forced to return that same Single anyway. Non-Single shapes (Multiple/Strided/TooLarge) differ only in which range limit produced them, and each caller re-applies its own fallback on cache HIT (jump has none by design: eval_next_addr turns any non-Single into CbExecutionError::Unsupported and defers to Python rather than pinning an arbitrary jump target). INVARIANT for a fourth entry point: it may share the cache only if (a) its Single results are pin-backed and (b) it re-applies its own fallback on HIT rather than trusting the stored shape. Keying is bv_cache_key, which must stay a FULL recursive op-tree hash (angr-owr37) — a shallow key silently cross-wires addresses.

Native VEX dirty-helper handlers in native/angr/src/vex/dirty.rs are ONLY reachable if ALL their args are concrete u64. statements_dirty.rs::handle_dirty_call (the IRStmt::Dirty branch) eval_expr_with_callbacks each arg first; the IRExpr::GSPTR | IRExpr::VECRET arm in expressions.rs::eval_expr_with_callbacks_inner returns NeedPythonFallback, propagating via ? before DirtyHelperDispatch::try_call runs. So any helper VEX invokes with a GSPTR arg (CPUID, RDTSCP) is DEAD CODE natively and must be handled by the Python engine — do NOT add native handlers for them. Reachable today: RDTSC (no args), IN/OUT (concrete port). angr-2iow measured zero GSPTR hits corpus-wide; angr-t1ok removed the dead CPUID/RDTSCP handlers. (angr-sqfj8.70: re-anchored from line refs ~L815/~L98 to symbol names after the inner/outer eval_expr split moved the arm.)

Generic divmod_double_to_single (now in native/angr/src/vex/ops/int_arith.rs after the ops.rs split; symbol-anchored) handles all VEX DivMod{U,S}{64to32,128to64} via dividend_w = 2*divisor_w. CONCRETE PATH -- CRITICAL: the concrete signed branch must sign-extend the dividend from its declared width to i128, NOT just 'value as i128' -- for divmod_64_to_32 the dividend's bit 63 IS its sign bit, but treating a u128 with high bits=0 as i128 always gives a positive number. Use sign_extend_low_to_i128(value, width). Same applies to the divisor (sign-extended from divisor_w). Result packing is (quotient | (remainder << divisor_w)) at dividend_w bits. SYMBOLIC PATH (was invariant-divmod-symbolic; both signed+unsigned IROp variants): extend divisor to dividend width using zero_extend for unsigned ops or sign_extend for signed, then udiv/sdiv + urem/srem on the extended pair, finally extract low N/2 bits of each and concat(remainder, quotient). Result format is low = quotient, high = remainder -- concat puts self in high, other in low, so concat(remainder, quotient). Z3's div/mod by zero is total and matches claripy, so no explicit zero guard is needed for the symbolic path.

INVARIANT (docs): a fix that adds a *guard* to a function used as a worked example in docs/ must update that example in the same commit. Two independent round-5 audit findings were this exact shape: docs/extending-angr/simprocedures.rst's 'Worked example 3: malloc' lost NativeMalloc's check_max(size, MAX_ALLOC_SIZE)? the moment angr-03vl4.53 added it (the section had been refreshed one commit earlier, for an unrelated reason, so 'recently touched' is no evidence of currency), and docs/extending-angr/rust_vex_ops.rst's BYPASS matrix kept a dead Iop_Perm8x32 opcode after angr-sqfj8.117 remapped the family. Why it is worse than ordinary doc rot: an example is *copied*, so a missing guard propagates the hole the guard closed into every new procedure written from it — stale prose merely misleads. Neither tools/check_line_citations.py nor any other CI gate can see this class (no line number, no symbol rename), so the only defense is the fix author grepping docs/ for the function/opcode name they just changed. Applies to any declare_proc!/register_procs! sample, VEX opcode table, or API snippet.

File splits/moves in native/angr/src/ re-red the baseline-audit gates (tools/check_line_citations.py and siblings): their baselines are keyed on <path>\t<comment-text>, so a line-number citation that was baselined under the OLD file reappears as a NEW violation under the new one, and the gate is only green again once you act on it. Preferred fix is to SYMBOL-ANCHOR the moved citation (cite the fn/struct it points at, per CLAUDE.md's symbol-anchor convention) and DELETE the old baseline row -- that shrinks the debt instead of relocating it. Repathing the row is the fallback when the target genuinely has no resolvable symbol; never reach for --update-baseline, which would silently re-add the row under the new path. Seen angr-c7xno.45 (expressions.rs -> expressions_inspect.rs) where two rows moved and both resolved to real Python symbols (SimSolver.Unconstrained, AddressConcretizationMixin._apply_concretization_strategies).

Splitting a big Rust module in this crate: the sibling <mod>_tests.rs file must be split along the SAME boundaries, and its section-comment markers are NOT trustworthy boundaries. In helpers_tests.rs (angr-9ke6b.76) the '// --- Timeout / LengthLimiter / LoopBound ---' banner covered ~460 lines that also contained the effective_pc tests and the whole materialize_deferred_forks block; slicing on the banners produced dangling doc comments ('error: expected item after doc comment') and cross-file fixture references. Reliable method: (1) list every top-level 'fn ' with line numbers and classify each by the symbol it exercises, not by the banner above it; (2) walk BACKWARD from each fn over contiguous ///, //, and #[..] lines to find the true block start; (3) after cutting, grep each new file's head/tail for a trailing doc comment or a leading orphaned fixture. Shared test fixtures (e.g. push_active_at) do not survive the split -- either move them with their only consumer or inline the one-off call; a #[cfg(test)] mod tests is private, so cross-module fixture sharing is not available without making the tests mod pub(crate). REGISTRATION (angr-12jjk.16): do NOT hand-write the old '#[cfg(test)] #[path=..] #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, reason=..)] mod x;' block -- since fe99f2553 every one of the ~117 sites goes through the crate-root 'test_submod!' macro_rules in lib.rs. Arms: test_submod!("file_tests.rs" => name) / test_submod!(name) for default file naming / a 'z3 ' prefix on either for the cfg(all(test, feature="vex-engine-z3")) gate. It is defined ahead of lib.rs's mod declarations so legacy textual macro scope reaches every module -- invoke it unqualified, and #[path] resolves relative to the INVOKING file (verified by the full cargo test --all-targets build). DOC DUPLICATION (angr-5mnx3.69): the extraction also leaves TWO copies of the submodule's op-set description — a doc comment on the 'mod X;' decl in the parent, and the file's own '//!' header — and a later move of individual ops between submodules updates only the file header. In vex/ops/mod.rs three decl comments (vec_int_arith, vec_compare, vec_permute_mul) still named families that had since migrated to the vec_int_lane_op driver, or omitted families the file had since gained; each file's own header was already correct. Nothing gates this (check_line_citations.py only sees line refs). So when moving an op between ops/*.rs submodules, grep the parent mod.rs for the 'mod <target>;' decl and fix that comment in the SAME commit; prefer keeping the decl comment about placement/visibility rationale and letting the file's //! header carry the op inventory, so there is only one copy to rot.

invariant: in native/angr/src/memory/, the page symbolic_bitmap and multi_bitmap are NOT mutually exclusive, and no code may assume they are. A byte promoted Symbolic->Multi keeps BOTH bits set: SymbolicMemory::set_multi_alternatives retires the symbolic_objects entry via retire_symbolic_object_at but never calls MemoryPage::clear_symbolic. Multi wins by DISPATCH ORDER instead -- every reader must probe Multi before Symbolic. Current readers that do: load_concrete_common's range_has_multi gate, assemble_load_with_multi, compute_wider_load_fingerprint, merge::merge_byte_value's is_multi arm. A new reader that checks is_symbolic first will silently resolve a Multi byte to a retired/absent symbolic object. Corollary for readers that only want CONCRETE bytes: is_symbolic alone is not enough, because a cell installed on a never-symbolic byte (install_multi_for_candidates) sets only the multi bit -- SymbolicMemory::read_concrete_bytes_for_lift has to check both, else the lifter decodes MultiPayload::collapse's don't-care concrete_byte default as an instruction byte (angr-4r8mh, fixed). The reverse transition IS asymmetric and must stay so: a symbolic store over a Multi cell DOES clear the multi bit (store_concrete -> clear_multi_at), because there the stale bit would win the dispatch order and shadow the fresh value (angr-0jh0j.31). Pinned by memory::tests::multi::payload::test_multi_supersedes_existing_symbolic, collapse.rs::test_symbolic_overwrite_clears_multi_cell and collapse.rs::test_lift_read_stops_at_multi_byte.

automaton epsilon-marker contract (angr-9ke6b.191, 2026-08-03): EpsilonNFA::move_on_symbol (native/angr/src/automaton/epsilon_nfa.rs) returns Result<StateSet, EpsilonSymbolError> — it used to assert!(!is_epsilon(symbol)). Reason the Result branch was chosen over the debug_assert! branch the bead also allowed: the ONLY caller chain is PyEpsilonNFA::minimize -> subset_construction -> move_on_symbol, i.e. it is entirely reachable from PyO3, where a Rust panic becomes an opaque PanicException in Python instead of a ValueError. Ripple was cheap (one non-test caller), so subset_construction now returns Result<DFA, EpsilonSymbolError> and PyEpsilonNFA::minimize maps it with PyValueError::new_err(err.to_string()). The invariant itself still holds by construction: EpsilonNFA::add_transition keeps EPSILON out of self.alphabet, and subset_construction only iterates nfa.alphabet(). Rule of thumb this establishes for the .9ke6b assert!-hardening band: pick Result over debug_assert! when the function is PyO3-reachable AND the caller count is small; pick debug_assert! (see angr-9ke6b.182 in dfa.rs) when it is a pure-internal worklist invariant.

eval_upto/eval_upto_wide (native/angr/src/symbolic/solving_ops.rs) return witnesses in CANONICAL ASCENDING ORDER as of angr-op0dn.10.1 (commit 3f5e2a782). As of angr-9ke6b.142 (commit 0277e87a6) the enumeration machinery — warm-model seed, exclude-loop, trailing sort_unstable — lives in ONE shared helper, SymContext::enumerate_distinct<T: Ord>(ast, n, extract, exclusion_of); the two public fns keep only their concrete fast paths, the deterministic-mode branch (eval_upto only), the query_class scope, and the closures. ExtractionError (native/angr/src/arch/calling_conventions.rs, re-exported from arch::mod) has exactly THREE variants: SpSymbolic (state.get_sp().as_u64() failed), StackUnmapped{arg_index,addr} (memory_load failed for that slot), RegisterOverflow{requested,available} (ABI has no stack window — syscall ABIs other than MIPS O32). There is ONE argument-extraction implementation: exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi, which walks a RustSimState using an ArgExtractAbi borrow; core_outcome_cc and helpers' extract_procedure_args/extract_syscall_args are thin adapters over it. Do NOT reintroduce a second copy on the CallingConvention trait — the old trait method extract_args (over a bare RegisterFile + Option<&SymbolicMemory>) and its MemoryUnavailable variant were DELETED in angr-9iny6 (2026-08-08) precisely because they were a structurally-parallel duplicate with no production caller, kept alive only by their own tests. CallingConvention now supplies ABI facts only (arg/syscall register windows, pointer_size, stack_arg_offset, return/link registers). Never fabricate silent placeholders on either the error or the register-overflow path: every failure must fall through to the Python callback.

FP-return calling convention: CallingConvention::fp_return_register() (native/angr/src/arch/calling_conventions.rs) is the single source of truth for where a scalar double return lands. Some(224)=xmm0 on SystemVAMD64, Some(320)=q0/v0 on AArch64, None everywhere else. The None reasons differ: x86 returns in the x87 st0 stack and ARM EABI soft-float in the r0:r1 integer pair (neither modelled); MIPS O32/N64 DO expose the register (mips32_off::F0/mips64_off::F0, aliased f0/$f0 in ALIASES_MIPS32/64) — the blocker is float-ABI-variant ambiguity, since a hard-float MIPS binary returns the double in $f0 but a -msoft-float build returns it in the $v0/$v1 integer pair and nothing in a RegisterFile distinguishes them. Same ambiguity that keeps MipsO32::fp_arg_registers deliberately empty. (Corrected angr-sqfj8.9: the older 'our register files do not expose $f0 yet' claim was false.) A native proc returning a double writes the 64-bit IEEE-754 bit pattern to the LOW 64 bits of that offset and must return Ok(None) to suppress the dispatcher's default integer-return store (see procedures/strtod.rs::NativeStrtod). To add a new FP-return arch: implement the trait method, do NOT hard-code an offset in the proc. Companion: cc_for_arch() is the non-panicking registry lookup — use it in procs that can defer to Python; default_cc_for_arch() keeps the loud panic for argument extraction, where a wrong CC would silently yield wrong-but-plausible args.

icicle.rs lives at native/angr/src/fuzzer/icicle.rs (moved there from the crate root in angr-fs8kb.85) and is behind the default-OFF `fuzzer` cargo feature — fuzzer.rs declares `pub(crate) mod icicle;` under lib.rs's #[cfg(feature = "fuzzer")] gate on `mod fuzzer`. Rust's `f32::max`/`f64::max` (and `min`) are NOT a drop-in for IEEE-754-2008 maxNum/minNum in VEX ops: they lower to LLVM `maxnum`, whose docs leave the ±0 case as 'may return either operand', while ARM's FPMax/FPMin — which VMAXNM/VMINNM (`Iop_MaxNumF32/64`, `Iop_MinNumF32/64`) defer to once NaNs are handled — pin maxNum(+0,-0)=+0 and minNum(+0,-0)=-0. Spell the concrete path out by hand: NaN operands first (return the *other* one — that is what makes it maxNum rather than max), then the `-0.0 == 0.0` tie, then the ordered compare. See `num_min_max` in `vex/ops/float_arith.rs`. Note also that the compare-and-select `FMin`/`FMax` lane ops in `vex/ops/lane_traits.rs` are a *different* op family with deliberately different NaN behaviour (SSE MINPS/MAXPS style: whichever operand the compare falls through to) — do not unify them. Symbolic side is fine: SMT-LIB `fp.max`/`fp.min` (Z3_mk_fpa_max/min) already carry the maxNum NaN contract and are exact, so no rounding mode is threaded. Sibling of invariant-rust-as-cast-is-rne-only.

Leak-gate self-test caught a bug in the GATE, not the engine (angr-c4xcs.4). A deliberate leak injector written as std::mem::forget(Box::new([0u8;64])) is ELIDED ENTIRELY by release-mode LLVM: the allocation is never read and never dropped, so it is dead code. Result: valgrind saw nothing, the self-test reported clean, and the leak gate was silently incapable of failing. Fix: Box::into_raw(vec![0u8;64].into_boxed_slice()) + std::hint::black_box(ptr) -- opaque to the optimizer, unreachable to memcheck, so it lands in 'definitely lost'. Now measures exactly 64.00 B/iter. See inject_leak() in native/angr/examples/leak_probe.rs. INVARIANT (generalized in angr-91vj9.7): any gate that can only report 'clean' -- leak, perf, or a baseline-gated LINT -- must ship a self-test that proves it can fail, and that self-test must run BEFORE the real check in CI. nightly-ci.yml::valgrind_leak_check and ci.yml's 'VEX rounding-mode threading audit' both do this; the latter's self_test() in tools/audit_rounding_mode_threading.py classifies a synthetic threaded/dropped-underscore/dropped-unused/exempt quartet, which matters most for a lint whose baseline is EMPTY -- it then passes vacuously on day one and nothing distinguishes 'no violations' from 'detector broken'.

Legacy (pre-LFS) stat-family syscall numbers must stay UNREGISTERED in the Rust native registry on every 32-bit arch: i386/ARM 106/107/108, MIPS32 4106/4107/4108. The Rust writers (write_i386_stat / write_arm_stat / write_mips32_stat, dispatched by write_stat_for_arch in syscalls/file_path/stat_layouts.rs) emit only the LFS 'struct stat64' layout used by the *64 numbers (195/196/197, 4213/4214/4215) — st_size at 0x30, 64-bit st_ino at 0x0C. Registering a legacy number to NativeStat/Lstat/FstatSyscall writes a correctly-sized but wrong-offset struct instead of falling back to Python, which DOES have procs for these numbers (angr's linux_kernel.py i386/arm/mips-o32 maps all define 106/107/108). angr-9ke6b.226 fixed exactly this for ARM 107. Older comments claiming 'angr's i386/arm maps have no legacy entry' were false — the correct rationale is the layout mismatch. mod_tests.rs::file_path_stubs_registered_on_all_arches now asserts all nine are absent.

native/angr/src/symbolic/local_constraints.rs (split out of context.rs by angr-fs8kb.35) holds a pub(super) LocalConstraints struct that combines both assumed (Vec<(RustBV, bool)>) and z3_assertions (Vec<z3::ast::Bool>, gated on vex-engine-z3) under one Mutex<LocalConstraints> field on SymContext. This replaced the prior two separate Mutex<Vec<...>> fields (assumed_constraints_local + z3_assertions_local). Why: hot path (assume_true/assume_false/add_constraint_raw) used to acquire 2 locks per call; now 1. How to apply: when adding new assumed/z3_assertion writes, lock once via self.local_constraints.lock() and access fields via .assumed and .z3_assertions. Reads should follow the same pattern; never reintroduce separate Mutexes for these two vectors. The shared Arc<Vec<...>> prefixes (assumed_constraints_shared / z3_assertions_shared) remain as separate fields -- only the local additions are combined. Fork-time freeze: snapshot_fork_ops.rs::freeze_into_shared<T: Clone> is the generic helper that replaced the prior two specialized fns (freeze_z3_assertions, freeze_assumed_constraints). It takes a &Mutex<Arc<Vec<T>>> shared prefix plus a &mut Vec<T> local -- the caller already holds the LocalConstraints lock and passes a mutable ref to the field. This avoids a redundant lock/unlock cycle inside fork() and lets fork freeze both vectors under one local-lock acquisition. Never re-introduce per-vector freeze fns or have freeze acquire the local Mutex itself -- SymContext::fork/merge (z3 and non-z3 paths) are the only callers, and they lock LocalConstraints once and pass &mut local.assumed and &mut local.z3_assertions. Cloning-vs-moving discipline: with scope_open=true (an open bare push/pop scope, i.e. bare_local_savepoints non-empty) freeze always clones, because the matching pop() must be able to truncate local; otherwise Arc::get_mut+append moves elements without per-element clones.

materialize_deferred_forks (exploration/fork_materialize.rs) is the single source of truth for the SERIAL deferred-fork pipeline: condition lookup -> reconstruct_deferred_fork_condition (condition_ast) -> conservative unconstrained fork -> build_unexplored_fork -> SAT split. Callers: step_one's find/avoid arm (run_loop.rs) + _resume_after_simprocedure / _deadend_pending_callback / _resume_after_symbolic_branch (resume.rs). Per-caller variation lives in MaterializeForkCtx: guard_sink (Some = continuing state receives the taken-path guard) and stats (Some iff profiling). set_root stays caller-side (needs &mut StateManager) and MUST be applied to BOTH the sat and unsat vectors — every legacy copy registered lineage before the SAT check. Two quirks preserved on purpose: run_loop + deadend DROP unsat forks (no pruned-stash push), and the batch timer is charged even for an EMPTY fork list. The parallel mirror materialize_deferred_forks_core (core_outcome_handlers.rs) is NOT folded in — no condition_ast fallback, fires the constraints inspect BP, atomics not ExecutionStats (angr-ph300.73).

LoadG (and any future VEX statement that reads memory) must call VEXInterpreter::load_layered / load_layered_at, NOT load_from_callback. load_from_callback is the LAST rung of the ladder: it only tries synthesize_unservable_load then the raw Python memory_load callback, skipping try_rust_memory_load, pending_stores, pending_symbolic_stores, all_flushed_stores and try_read_concrete_memory. In production use_rust_memory=true and stores are never synced to Python (statements_store.rs 'Rust owns memory'), so a direct load_from_callback reads stale/unrelated data for any address written earlier in the same step. angr-9ke6b.83 fixed this for LoadG by extracting eval_load's ladder into load_layered (expressions_loads.rs) and calling it from resolve_loadg_load. Regression tests: statements_tests.rs loadg_sees_pending_store_from_same_block / loadg_sees_rust_memory_store_from_same_block / loadg_single_concretization_sees_rust_memory_store.

RustSimState::merge (native/angr/src/state/fork.rs::merge) resolves overlay-map key conflicts by earlier-wins iteration order: self > earlier-other > later-other. All three overlay maps (symbolic_pages, hook_symbolic_memory, addr_to_ast) share the identical union loop that only inserts a key if !contains_key, so the FIRST branch to own a key wins. A 2-state test cannot distinguish this from later-wins; needs >=3 states where a conflicting key lives in two DIFFERENT others but not self. Covered by state/tests/merge_multi_state.rs::test_merge_three_state_overlay_union_and_tiebreak (angr-qwyti.2/n0irt.18): tag entries by provenance (size field for hook/addr_to_ast, int AST value for symbolic_pages) so a reversed others fold flips the merged tag and fails. stdin_symbols unions with dedup-by-name, self-order-first.

MIPS Linux syscalls report error in $a3 (0=ok, non-zero=err) separately from $v0 return; glibc branches on it. Rust dispatcher must mirror angr's linux_syscall_update_error_reg: when unsigned ret >= SYSCALL_ERRNO_START (-1133 for both O32/N64), set error_reg=all-ones and ret=-ret (positive errno); else error_reg=0, ret passthrough. $a3 VEX offsets: 36 (MIPS32, base 8 + 7*4), 72 (MIPS64, base 16 + 7*8). Implemented via CallingConvention::syscall_error_register()->Option<(offset, errno_start)> in arch/calling_conventions.rs + CcSnapshot::write_syscall_return() in exploration/core_outcome_cc.rs (angr-pfbu; the fn moved out of stepping.rs with the angr-nbim4.3 post-step-core split). Pinned since angr-5mnx3.4 by calling_conventions_tests::test_syscall_error_register_only_on_mips_and_names_a3 (the tuple: $a3 by name on MIPS, None everywhere else) and core_outcome_tests/syscall_dispatch.rs::write_syscall_return_splits_errno_flag_into_a3_on_mips (the behaviour, incl. the inclusive errno_start boundary) plus its _passes_through_on_abis_without_an_error_register control.

invariant-on-state-removed-notify-sites addendum (angr-0jh0j.13): the notify inventory must include BULK-REPLACE paths, not just per-state removals. manager_methods_snapshot.rs::load_snapshot_bytes overwrites self.sm wholesale and removes no state individually, so a removal-site grep/audit (angr-myzjx.25's 'all 7 sites') could not see it; it now iterates self.sm.state_ids(STASH_ACTIVE) and notifies before the swap, AFTER steady_config_guard() so states that guard drains back into active are covered. The mirror arrival side is deliberately NOT routed through push_active/on_fork (unlike helpers.rs::push_to_stash for the Python move/insert APIs): a snapshot restore is a whole-world replacement whose active-deque order the dump preserved on purpose, and a lazily-memoizing policy populates its side table on the next select, so there is nothing to leak on arrival.

INVARIANT (page-granular moves vs flat side tables): MemoryPage carries only data + symbolic_bitmap + multi_bitmap. The per-address payloads (SymbolicMemory::symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects, multi_versions) are FLAT maps on SymbolicMemory, not nested in the page — so any path that inserts/clones/adopts a whole page from another SymbolicMemory (merge's (None,Some(op)) arm, snapshot restore, migration, prefetch) must copy the matching side-table entries explicitly or it installs bitmap bits pointing at nothing. Orphaned Multi bits are especially bad: range_has_multi (load.rs) gates on multi_objects, NOT the bitmap, so the load silently returns the stale concrete byte, and merge's 's_multi implies a payload' expect panics on the next merge. Fixed for merge in angr-c7xno.50 by walking MemoryPage::multi_offsets (mirrors symbolic_offsets) and routing payloads through the existing multi_ops queue so set_multi_alternatives does the bitmap sync + bump_multi_version. Note this is the inverse direction of invariant-page-bitmap-authoritative: the bitmap is authoritative for READS, but it is not self-sufficient for MOVES.

Any Vec::with_capacity / reserve whose count crosses the PyO3 boundary must be bounded BEFORE the reservation. This crate is panic=abort, so both failure modes are uncatchable process aborts, not Rust errors a caller can handle: 'capacity overflow' panics when count*size_of::<T>() exceeds isize, and alloc::handle_alloc_error aborts for a huge-but-not-overflowing count. No guest input is needed — an ordinary documented Python call (RustExplorationManager::register_simprocedure with a bogus num_args) is enough. Two fix shapes, pick by whether the refusal should degrade or raise. (a) Degrade: a named MAX_* const next to the error enum + a new error variant returned before the reservation, so the caller falls back (native dispatcher -> Python SimProcedure) instead of crashing — arch::MAX_EXTRACT_ARGS / ExtractionError::TooManyArgs guarding exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi (angr-0jh0j.23). (b) Raise at the trust boundary: a MAX_* const + a check_*(op, n) -> Result<(), String> guard called by every Python-facing entry point, message-typed rather than error-typed so the layer defining it stays pyo3-free and callers reporting through different channels (PyValueError vs BridgeError) can share it — symbolic::width_guards::check_bv_width is the precedent, symbolic::bv_chunk::check_concrete_load_size / MAX_CONCRETE_LOAD_BYTES the second instance (angr-0jh0j.11). Shape (b) is what a *generic* helper wants when it cannot construct its own error type E: guard at the boundaries, and additionally cap the helper's own reservation (Vec::with_capacity(n.min(MAX)) — bounds the allocation without truncating the result, since the loop still grows the vec as data arrives) as defence in depth for future callers. A bound like this also retroactively makes downstream index arithmetic (i * ptr_size) provably non-overflowing.

SURPRISE (angr-9ke6b.50): enabling pyo3's 'multiple-pymethods' feature UNMASKS 391 unreachable_pub warnings crate-wide, instantly reddening the CI clippy -D warnings gate (lib.rs has #![warn(unreachable_pub)] from angr-9ke6b.214). Verified empirically both ways: 0 hits at HEAD without the feature, 391 with it, split across solver.rs(78), callbacks/mod.rs(56), segmentlist.rs(27), the manager_methods*.rs files, callbacks/config.rs, automaton/python_bindings.rs. Mechanism: pyo3's NON-multiple-pymethods codegen was masking the lint on every #[pymethods] method AND on the #[pyclass] struct those blocks belong to. So the lint never actually covered the pyo3 surface -- the flip does not create new over-broad pubs, it reveals pre-existing ones. FIX CHOSEN: a scoped #[allow(unreachable_pub, reason=...)] on each affected #[pymethods] impl block and #[pyclass] struct (16 files, ~25 attributes), which restores EXACTLY the pre-feature coverage. Rejected alternative: rewriting 391 'pub fn' -> 'pub(crate) fn' (mechanically safe -- unreachable_pub proves external targets cannot reach them -- but a ~400-line diff mixing two concerns, and it risks a second dead_code wave). Do NOT blanket-allow unreachable_pub at crate level; that kills the guardrail for real Rust API surface. Note the pyclass STRUCT needs its own allow separately from its #[pymethods] block.

Convention for pyo3 items flagged by unreachable_pub (angr-9ke6b.50, lib.rs 'unreachable_pub' note): a #[pyclass] struct or #[pymethods] impl block that trips the lint gets a scoped #[allow(unreachable_pub, reason = "pyo3 ...")] with the VERBATIM reason string used in segmentlist.rs/solver.rs -- do NOT narrow it to pub(crate). Rationale: those items are reached from Python, not Rust, so their Rust visibility is decorative, and the allow restores exactly the coverage pyo3's pre-multiple-pymethods codegen used to mask. Narrowing works and clippy goes green either way, so the wrong fix is easy to land; check the existing allow sites before choosing. Non-pyo3 items keep the opposite rule (narrow to pub(crate), angr-9ke6b.214) so dead_code can see them.

Overflow-guard regression tests must pick operands whose WRAPPING product/sum is benign, not merely huge — otherwise the test passes under both spellings and pins nothing. For a saturating_mul size*count guard, u64::MAX*2 is the wrong choice (wraps to u64::MAX-1, still over the cap, so the oversize branch fires either way); 2^63*2 is right (wraps to exactly 0, which takes the zero-total early-return and reports a successful no-op for a 2^64-byte request). Canonical pair: procedures/fwrite_tests.rs::test_fwrite_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping and procedures/fread_tests.rs::test_fread_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping (angr-0jh0j.40/.43). Always mutation-check: swap saturating_mul -> wrapping_mul, confirm the new test FAILS, revert. Release builds set no overflow-checks so the wrapping result is what ships; a checked-profile panic is a second, weaker net.

SymContext::next_id (native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_id_ops.rs) allocates from the PROCESS-GLOBAL NEXT_SYMBOL_ID atomic, not a per-context counter. Any Rust unit test asserting that two consecutive next_id() draws are ADJACENT (b == a + 1) is flaky under cargo test parallelism -- another test can take the id in between. This sank the iter203 ralph gate via symbolic::context::context_tests_lineage::test_fork (left 9732, right 9731). Assert strict monotonicity (b > a) instead; fork's real contract is 'keeps drawing from the same global sequence', not 'next id is exactly parent+1'. Fixed in angr-lzywj.

run_loop_parallel_wave + run_loop_parallel_steady found early-return (found_count()>=num_find at loop top) must call flush_parked_bounces_to_active BEFORE returning ExplorationEvent::found, else a bounce tail parked in pending_parallel_bounces by a prior wave (states in NO stash) is stranded — active_count() under-reports vs the serial loop which leaves the equivalent frontier in STASH_ACTIVE. Steady loop flushes AFTER finalize_steady_session so the resident-id guard in flush_parked_bounces_to_active sees the drained frontier and never double-inserts. Distinct trigger from angr-05kiw (single-threaded fallback stranding). Fixed angr-ph300.8, commit cd8165d1d.

Parallel-loop shared-context construction is DRY as of angr-ph300.12 (commit 003ee59b6): ParallelShared::seeded(found_count, num_find) is the ONLY place a ParallelShared literal is built, and RustExplorationManager::build_parallel_process(callbacks, prof, shared) is the ONLY place the Box<ProcessFn> wrapping parallel_process_state is assembled — used by both run_loop_parallel_wave (per-wave, run_loop_wave.rs) and ensure_steady_session (per-session, run_loop_steady.rs). finalize_steady_session no longer hand-inlines the stepped.swap + CoreCounters drain; it calls fold_parallel_shared_counters, the same helper the wave loop uses, so wave and steady counter semantics cannot drift. INVARIANT for future work: add a new ParallelShared field by seeding it in ::seeded (not at a call site), and clone PythonCallbacks on the GIL thread BEFORE calling build_parallel_process (Py<T>::clone needs the GIL and must never run on a worker).

RegisterFile::merge (native/angr/src/arch/register_file.rs) width-mismatch merge, angr-9ke6b.13: when two forked paths hold symbolic values of DIFFERENT widths at the same register offset (path A wrote eax/32-bit, path B wrote rax/64-bit at the same VEX offset), the merge used to keep self's value and drop other's — an unsound merge. Fix: widen BOTH sides to max(width) by calling RegisterFile::get(offset, size, ctx) on each file (get composes that file's own symbolic overlay with its own concrete backing bytes, so this is DRY — no hand-rolled zero-extend), then ITE at the common width, and drop overlays strictly INSIDE the widened span the same way put does. TRAP that forced a restructure: the merge loop iterates a HashSet<u32> of offsets, so mutating self.symbolic mid-loop while the widening arm READS self via get() would make the result depend on iteration order — merged values are now staged into a Vec and applied after the loop. Tests: merge_width_mismatch_ite_merges_both_paths (mock ctx, walks the expr tree via RustBV::operands() — Debug on RustBV prints 'Expression(Ite, 64, 3 operands)' and does NOT render operand symbol names, so a format!("{:?}") substring check silently fails) and merge_width_mismatch_selects_each_path_under_solver (real SymContext + push/add_constraint/is_sat/pop).

RegisterFile (native/angr/src/arch/mod.rs) stores registers as data: Arc<Vec<u8>> (NOT Vec<u8>) since angr-6t8z3.1. fork()/derived Clone share the buffer O(1) via Arc::clone; the deep copy happens lazily on first write. EVERY &mut self register write MUST route through Arc::make_mut(&mut self.data) or it will silently leak across the fork boundary (CoW broken). Current write sites: put()'s three concrete-write loops + copy_from_bytes(). set_ip/set_sp delegate to put; merge mutates only self.symbolic. Reads index self.data[..] directly (Deref). Serde shadow RegisterFileData.data stays Vec<u8>: From<RegisterFile> uses Arc::unwrap_or_clone, From<RegisterFileData> wraps Arc::new. Faithfulness gate: test_register_file_fork_cow_isolation in arch/register_file_tests.rs. Measured state_fork bench -9.6%. Extends invariant-symbolic-memory-fork-fields CoW discipline to registers.

RustBV IR rewrites can be bypassed: extract_into / truncate_into / extract_no_ctx all exist as ways to construct Extract nodes in value.rs. Only extract_into runs the canonicalization rules (Rule 1-5 at value.rs:1540-1605). truncate_into (used heavily by vex/ops.rs at 309, 356, 3023) and extract_no_ctx (used by arch/register_file.rs register slicing) build BVOp::Extract directly. Any IR rewrite that only fires inside extract_into therefore has a coverage gap. The fix from angr-p8cz: add a second hook point at Z3 emission (emit_extract_z3_cached in value.rs) that re-applies the rules. Pattern for future rewrite additions: hook at BOTH construction (extract_into) AND emission (emit_extract_z3_cached) to be self-correcting.

ObjectMapper identity in native/angr/src/automaton/python_bindings.rs (angr-9ke6b.187, 2026-08-01; interner extracted in .186, 2026-08-02): identity is bucket-by-hash() + PyAny::eq disambiguation via fn find_in_bucket, NOT the old (hash, repr) tuple key. Invariant for future edits: never reintroduce repr() (or any stringification) as an equality proxy — it silently merges __eq__-distinct NFA/DFA states/symbols. Both sides now share one struct IdInterner (fields: buckets, interned, reserved, kind); ObjectMapper holds `states` and `symbols` IdInterners and its get_or_create_state_id / get_or_create_symbol_id / lookup_symbol are thin delegators. StateId and SymbolId are both u32, so one interner serves both; the symbol side's only difference is reserved=Some(EPSILON), which IdInterner::get_or_create turns into the 'Too many symbols' error. RENAMED 2026-08-03 (angr-9ke6b.190): IdInterner::get -> IdInterner::lookup and ObjectMapper::get_symbol_by_id -> ObjectMapper::lookup_symbol, both now returning enum IdLookup { Found(&Py<PyAny>), Reserved, Unassigned } instead of Option — the old Option collapsed 'this is the EPSILON sentinel' and 'this id was never interned', two different bugs, into one None that DFA::to_networkx could not tell apart. Keep them distinct; tests use the test-local expect_found helper rather than a method on IdLookup. Test gotcha in python_bindings_tests.rs: py.run() snippets get a locals dict but globals=None, so a class method cannot see its own class name — use type(other) is type(self), not isinstance(other, ClassName).

NativeSimProcedure::name() returns &'static str. For a procedure whose name is only known at runtime (Python-registered hooks, ReturnUnconstrained stubs), leak the String in the *constructor* and store the resulting &'static str in the field -- do NOT keep a String field and Box::leak inside name(), which leaks a fresh allocation on every call. Canonical sites: procedures/python_proc.rs::PythonNativeProcedure::new and procedures/stub.rs::NativeReturnUnconstrained::new. The leak is bounded (one allocation per registered procedure, process lifetime) and the registry holds an Arc<Self> anyway. For names that repeat (unmapped VEX opcodes), intern instead -- vex/opcode_map.rs::intern_unmapped_op. angr-91vj9.10.

Iop_QDMull16Sx4/32Sx2 (signed doubling saturating widening multiply, NEON VQDMULL, (I64,I64)->V128) map to IROp::VQDMull{elem,count} in vex/opcode_map_vector.rs (parse_vector). Implemented by vec_qdmull in ops/vec_permute_mul.rs: same full-lane widening layout as vec_mull (even=false, always signed), plus *2 and signed saturation to 2N bits. Saturation only fires on MIN*MIN (both -2^(N-1)): doubled product 2^(2N-1) clamps to 2^(2N-1)-1. Symbolic path widens inputs to out_width+2 bits before doubling to avoid overflow, then reuses saturate_lane_symbolic (widened to pub(super) in ops/vec_saturate.rs). Only 16Sx4/32Sx2 exist in libVEX; the QDMulHi/QRDMulHi high-half family is still unmapped.

RustBV::Concrete is u128-backed (max 128 bits). Any Python->Rust memory or register sync that takes 'data: &[u8]' and packs all bytes into a u128 via 'value |= (b as u128) << (i * 8)' is BUGGY for data.len() > 16. In release mode, shifts >= 128 mask to 7 bits — bytes 16..31 OR back into low bytes, then store_concrete's page-fill loop replays the same masking, painting a 16-byte-repeating pattern across the claimed width. Found via angr-5aj8 (2026-06-06): baby-re under ANGR_RUST_USE_CALLBACK_MEMORY_PROXY=1 corrupted stack with witness pattern. Safe pattern: split into 16-byte chunks per RustSimState::apply_changes in state.rs (loop 'while offset < bytes.len(): chunk_size = remaining.min(16); ...'). Fixed sites: _set_state_memory_concrete (state_api.rs), _pending_memory_store (pending_api.rs), RustSimState::memory_store (state.rs). REMAINING SITES TO AUDIT: register-write path in apply_changes (state.rs:2294-2301) does NOT chunk — would corrupt YMM (32B) / ZMM (64B) wide-register writes. claripy_bridge.rs:1865 'bytes_to_u128' has 'if i < 16' guard so it just drops high bytes (less catastrophic but still wrong).

Rustdoc rule (3) addendum (angr-f9pct, 2026-08-09): --document-private-items makes rustdoc *document* private items but does NOT make them *linkable* from outside their privacy scope — intra-doc links use ordinary Rust name resolution, so [`crate::exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi`] fails with 'no item named helpers in module exploration' because `mod helpers;` is private to `exploration`. There is a second, distinct failure mode in the same lane: a link that DOES resolve but whose target is less visible than the documented item trips rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links (e.g. pub `add_constraint_raw` -> private `install_constraint`). Both classes get a plain code span; never widen visibility and never add a per-site #[allow]. See invariant-rustdoc-intra-doc-links for the base rules.

format_common::read_format_string (procedures/) is the single home for reading a printf/scanf-family format string: it delegates to strings::scan_concrete_bounded bounded by MAX_FORMAT_LEN, so memory_load faults and symbolic bytes propagate as Err (Python fallback) rather than the old 'Err(_) => break' silent-truncation that committed symbolic stores on a corrupted format. It takes &mut RustSimState (scan_concrete_bounded needs it). extract_concrete_arg on a symbolic format byte already errored via ?; only the memory_load-failure path was swallowed. Formerly two private copies, scanf.rs::read_format_string and sprintf.rs::read_string, merged in angr-0jh0j.44 — a %s conversion argument is NOT a format string and scans against strings::MAX_STRING_SCAN instead.

scanf/printf length modifiers: BOTH consumers must resolve conversion width through LengthModifier::int_conv_bits(arch_bits) in procedures/format_common.rs — parse_scanf_format (procedures/scanf_spec.rs, takes arch_bits) and the sprintf-side parse_conversion_spec/render_conversion pair (procedures/sprintf_spec.rs + sprintf_conv.rs, reads state.arch().bits() once). Widths mirror format_parser.py int_len_mod's sim_types: hh->8, h->16, none->32, ll/j->64 always (SimTypeLongLong), l/z/t->arch_bits (SimTypeLong / SimTypeLength, so 32 on ILP32 x86/arm32). Two failure modes if this is hardcoded: ScanfSpec.bits drives state.memory_store(ptr, sym_val) (writes bits/8 bytes) and record_stdin_symbol, so an over-wide bits silently clobbers adjacent guest bytes with unconstrained symbols; on the sprintf side an over-wide mask renders %ld of a bit-31-set value as the zero-extended 64-bit number where Python prints the sign-folded 32-bit one. Regression test patterns: assert_scanf_store_width_arch in scanf_tests.rs (pre-fills 8 concrete 0xAA guard bytes, asserts exactly N low bytes symbolic and the rest still 0xAA) and sprintf_one_arch in sprintf_tests.rs; both take an arch string so ILP32 is covered. Fixed in 4a1dcf6fd (angr-vfhyx, hh/h) and angr-9ke6b.111 (l/z/t arch width).

VEX opcode parsing has exactly ONE entry point: the string-based parse_opcode in vex/opcode_map.rs. There is no numeric/u32 opcode table (parse_opcode_from_u32 was deleted). The native libVEX FFI lifter (vex/libvex_lifter.rs::c_op) converts its IROp discriminant back to the pyvex name via libvex_ffi.rs::enum_names::irop_name (generated by build.rs::generate_pyvex_ffi_enum_names from the vendored cdef, never hand-edited) and then calls parse_opcode; an unknown discriminant becomes the synthetic name Iop_UNKNOWN_<n>. Consequence: adding one string arm covers BOTH lifters — there is no second table to keep in sync. Same shape as parse_type (see invariant-parse-type-width-not-none).

Zero-length-hook skip tokens are a true LIFO stack, not a set. Consumption lives in ONE place: RustExplorationManager::consume_skip_hook (exploration/pending_api.rs), called from step_one in run_loop_single.rs. It expires stale entries (expiry <= steps) then pops only the topmost match via rposition+remove. Do NOT reintroduce a retain()-based removal there: _set_skip_hook_addr pushes without dedup, so nested zero-length hooks at the same PC hold multiple tokens, and a blanket retain collapses them all at once, leaving the second occurrence unskipped and re-arming the infinite loop the skip stack prevents (angr-9ke6b.47). _clear_skip_hook_for_addr intentionally KEEPS clear-all semantics -- it is an explicit Python-side reset, not a consumption. A non-empty skip_hook_stack also forces must_run_serial (angr-04tw3.1), since no parallel path consumes it -- which is why a leaked entry is not harmless and why load_snapshot_bytes clears the stack (angr-0jh0j.12, see invariant-snapshot-load-pending-world-teardown). (The pre-bd 'GAP 6' label this mechanism used to carry was stripped in angr-6cp06.17.)

Snapshot dump/load must be SYMMETRIC on the finalize contract. dump_snapshot_bytes (manager_methods_snapshot.rs, renamed from manager_methods_stats.rs in angr-03vl4.25) calls steady_config_guard() + flush_parked_bounces_to_active() before serializing self.sm; load_snapshot_bytes (angr-ph300.21), its sibling in the same module, must equally steady_config_guard() and clear pending_callbacks / pending_parallel_bounces / current_stepping_state_id BEFORE swapping self.sm. Otherwise the next run() finalizes the OLD steady session into the RESTORED stashes (two explorations merged) and a parked need_callback can resume a discarded pre-load state. Any future field added to the parked/pending set (things referencing live/worker states outside a stash) must be cleared here too. Regression: test_load_snapshot_clears_parked_pending_callback in test_manager_core.py parks a callback via symbolic SimProc arg then asserts pending_callback_ids() empty post-load.

Symbolic clz/ctz/popcount export from Rust->claripy MUST be tied to the operand AST, not a fresh BVS. claripy_bridge/export/ast_helpers.rs::build_sound_bitcount (moved there by the angr-5mnx3.11 split; was claripy_bridge/export.rs post zel8z.5, and claripy_bridge.rs before that) emits a sound encoding for width<=64: nested If(Extract(i,i,operand)==1, count, ...) for clz (LSB->MSB so MSB test is outermost) and ctz (MSB->LSB so LSB test is outermost); popcount is sum of ZeroExt(w-1, Extract(i,i,operand)). Result width == operand width (matches the concrete BVV(result,width) fast path). width>64 keeps the fresh-BVS fallback (record_export_unconstrained_clz). Pre-fix a fresh unconstrained BVS per call meant Python-side eval could return Rust-infeasible values AND identity was unstable. See angr-acoq.

Native SimProcedures returning a symbolic result must return at arch.bits() width (state.arch().bits()), not at any intermediate width. The concrete path goes through the procedures::arch_word(state, value: u64) helper (defined next to check_max in procedures/mod.rs, angr-12jjk.23) — do NOT hand-write RustBV::concrete(v as u128, state.arch().bits()) at a new call site. Symbolic path must zero-extend the predicate/byte to the same width to keep CFG/register sync invariants intact.

sync_constraints_from_python (exploration/constraint_sync.rs) has TWO SAT gates and the second is unreachable under the vex-engine-z3 feature: the unconditional post-sync check SAT-checks every time and returns Ok(false) on UNSAT, so by the time control reaches the partial-sync re-check (which re-checks only when failed_count>0 && success_count>0) the state is already known SAT. The re-check is defence-in-depth for a build where the unconditional check is compiled out -- do not write a test that claims to distinguish them. sync_constraints_partial_failure_unsat_is_pruned (helpers_tests.rs) pins the OBSERVABLE contract (partial conversion + contradictory constraints => Ok(false) => resume.rs prunes), not which gate fires.

Arg-count-guard convention in native/angr/src/syscalls/: every NativeSyscall::call starts with 'if args.len() < N' where N == the handler's own num_args() and == the number in the 'expected N args, got {}' message. The guard is defensive only — core_outcome_handlers.rs's dispatcher extracts exactly handler.num_args() args before calling, so a short slice is only reachable from direct unit-test calls. angr-9ke6b.156 (commit e858d1d67) fixed the last outlier (NativeFutexSyscall guarded at 2 while declaring 6). When adding a handler, keep all three numbers in sync.

Native syscall handlers must NOT mint symbolic returns with fixed names via RustBV::symbolic: z3::ast::BV::new_const(name,sort) returns the SAME Z3 constant for identical name+sort, so two time()/stub calls on one path are solver-equal (ret1!=ret2 UNSAT), unlike claripy BVS. Fix: syscalls::fresh_symbolic(ctx,prefix,width) appends procedures::symbol_counter(prefix). Test solver-distinctness (assert ret1!=ret2 is SAT via a fresh z3::Solver), NOT just distinct RustBV ids. angr-8o7w. The procedures side has TWO helpers over the same symbol_counter: use them rather than re-spelling the mint by hand. syscalls::support::fresh_symbolic for a plain mint, and procedures::fresh_zero_extended_symbol(state, prefix, src_bits, ext_bits) for the 'unconstrained value narrower than the C return type' shape (rand: 31->32, system: 8->32). Note ext_bits is the TOTAL target width for RustBV::zero_extend, while claripy's zero_extend takes the count of ADDED bits -- which is why the Python procs read zero_extend(sizeof(int) - 8) for the same thing (angr-6cp06.13).

SyscallOutcome::ContinueSymbolic { ret: RustBV } added 2026-05-08 to native/angr/src/syscalls/support.rs (re-exported as syscalls::SyscallOutcome) for syscalls returning a symbolic value via the return register (rax on amd64). Dispatcher in exploration/stepping.rs writes the BV directly with set_register_by_offset(ret_reg, ret) — no concrete wrap. Use this for time(2), and for any future syscall whose canonical Python procedure constructs a fresh BVS as its return value.

python_vex_op_fallback_count / python_vex_{unop,binop,triop,qop}_fallback_count (define_execution_stats! invocation in interpreter/execution_stats.rs — split out of interpreter/mod.rs in angr-9ke6b.91; ExecutionStats is still re-exported as crate::interpreter::ExecutionStats) must be bumped by EVERY arm that returns CbExecutionError::NeedPythonFallback for an op evaluation — including eval_binop's is_dispatch_fabricate_family arm (VPerm/Pclmul*/Crc32C), which cannot route through VEXInterpreter::vex_op_fallback because that helper hard-errors on all-concrete args and honors the ANGR_RUST_FABRICATE_UNSUPPORTED_IROP opt-in, both of which the family deliberately bypasses. So it increments the two counters inline instead. Do NOT 'simplify' that back to a bare Err(NeedPythonFallback) — angr-9ke6b.85 fixed exactly that undercount. vex_bypass_fabricate_count is a DIFFERENT counter and stays 0 for this family. Guard test: expressions_tests.rs::eval_binop_dispatch_fabricate_family_counts_as_python_fallback.

worker_thread (native/angr/src/exploration/scheduler_pool.rs since the angr-9ke6b.59 split; was scheduler.rs) MUST call clear_worker_local_caches() before it returns (before its local z3ctx drops). Workers populate the bridge thread-local AST_CACHE with RustBV values whose z3 ASTs are bound to z3ctx (via claripy_to_rustbv on interpreter paths). Rust runs thread_local! destructors at thread teardown AFTER z3ctx (a local) has dropped, so without the explicit clear those RustBVs dec_ref against a freed Z3 context (UAF — the angr-bjk8 hazard). The clear runs while z3ctx is still the live thread-local context. Do NOT remove this call. Pinned by test_worker_local_clear_empties_ast_cache (cache_tests.rs). Fixed in commit 89526a569 (angr-bjk8/angr-1yge9.9). See z3-context-rc-no-uaf-on-teardown for the corrected framing.

SymbolicMemory page-range calc (native/angr/src/memory/mod.rs): the exclusive-end formula end_page=ceil((addr+size)/PAGE_SIZE) OVERSHOOTS start_page by one page when size==0 AND addr is non-page-aligned, spuriously (un)mapping a page. Python's paged_memory_mixin loop never runs for length==0 -> always a true no-op. Fixed in map()/unmap() (angr-n0irt.5) via early 'if size==0 { return; }'. add_lazy_region() calls the same end_page_exclusive helper and is still NOT size==0-guarded — latent only (callers pass real cle segment sizes, never 0); add the guard there if it ever becomes reachable with size==0. Distinct from the overflow/underflow rules in [invariant-end-page-inclusive-zero-size], which the helper itself now enforces.

Sibling test-module naming convention: the recipe in rust-mod-tests-sibling-extraction originally emitted 'mod tests;' as the identifier, which left a directory-wide inconsistency. Canonical form is now '#[cfg(test)]\n#[path = "<file>_tests.rs"]\nmod <file>_tests;' — identifier matches the sibling file name, and the #[path] attribute is kept even though it is redundant (all 22 files in native/angr/src/syscalls/ do this). Rationale: grepping for the owning module name finds the parent file. angr-9ke6b.159 (commit 6f725cb68) fixed the last 7 stragglers in syscalls/ (exit, munmap, concurrency, identity, sigaction, memory_extras, signals). Nothing references these mods by path, so the rename is safe and test-only; no pip rebuild needed.

In Rust unit tests, RustSimState::memory_store (state/memory.rs) does NOT auto-map: storing to an unmapped page returns MemoryError::Unmapped despite the doc-comment mentioning an 'auto-mapping store'. Call map_memory(addr,size,perm) / map_memory_data first. Pattern used in state/tests/export.rs export_full tests (angr-n0irt.17): map_memory then memory_store a RustBV::symbolic to populate page symbolic_offsets. build_populated_state() (state/tests/helpers.rs, cfg vex-engine-z3) is the canonical fully-populated fixture for export/snapshot tests.
